5.1. Datasets
To comprehensively  evaluate  the performance  of our proposed  
method,  we conduct  experiments  on three publicly  available  medical  
image segmentation  datasets:  MMWHS17  (Gao et al., 2023 ) for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation,  BraTS21  (Han et al., 2021 ) 
for cross-sequence  brain glioma segmentation,  and PROMISE12  (Liu 
et al., 2020 ) for cross-site  prostate  segmentation.
(1) MMWHS17  Dataset:  The Multi-Modality  Whole Heart Segmen-
tation Challenge  2017 (MMWHS17)  dataset  is employed  for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation.  The dataset  contains  20 
MRI and 20 CT scans with corresponding  voxel-wise  annotations.  Fol-
lowing the experimental  setup in Zheng et al. (2024 ), we focus on four 
cardiac  structures:  ascending  aorta (AA), left atrium blood cavity (LAC), 
left ventricle  blood cavity (LVC), and left ventricle  myocardium  (MYO).  
We employ  a two-fold  cross-validation  strategy,  with 20 source domain  
scans and 10 target domain  scans for training,  and the remaining  10 
target scans for testing.  All scans are reoriented  to RAI orientation,  
cropped  to 128 × 128 × 128 voxels, and intensity-normalized  (CT: -
100 to 800 HU; MRI: 0.5th to 99.5th percentiles).  Bidirectional  domain  
adaptation  is performed  by alternating  MRI and CT as source domains.
(2) BraTS21  Dataset:  The BraTS21  Dataset  comprises  1251 MRI 
scans, each including  four modality  sequences  (T1, T1ce, T2, and 
FLAIR) and annotated  with tumor sub-regions.  To address  the distinct  
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences

tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences  
are chosen for bidirectional  domain  adaptation,  focusing  on the seg-

500 scans per domain  for source and target training,  with an additional  
251 cases allocated  for validation  and testing.  All volumes  are pre-

(3) PROMISE12  Dataset:  The PROMISE12  challenge  dataset  is used

and perform  two-fold  cross-validation.  For preprocessing,  we manually  
crop the original  scans to focus on the prostate  region and resize all 
cropped  scans to 256 × 256 × 32 with RAI orientation.
5.2. Experimental  setup and evaluation  metrics
Implementation  details:  Experiments  were conducted  on an NVIDIA  
RTX 3090 GPU with 24 GB memory.  The model was implemented  in 
PyTorch  and optimized  using the Adam optimizer.  We adopted  a 3D 
U-Net as the encoder,  with the channel  configuration  for each layer set 
to [8, 16, 32, 64]. The pixel-wise  segmentation  decoder  comprises  two 
ResNet blocks and a convolutional  layer, where the output channels  
match the number  of classes.  To balance  training  stability  and adap-
tation efficiency,  we applied  differentiated  learning  rates: 1 × 10−4 for 
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder

(FAUDA-Net  and DDSP),  we followed  the training  setting of DDSP, us-
ing 500 epochs.  Although  the core architectures  and parameter  counts 
naturally  differ between  2D and 3D networks,  we reproduced  the 
baselines  in the same computing  environment  as proposed  in their 
original  work.
Evaluation  metrics:  To evaluate  segmentation  quality,  we employed  
two complementary  evaluation  criteria:  the Dice Similarity  Coefficient  
(DSC) and Average  Surface  Distance  (ASD). DSC quantifies  the spatial 
agreement  between  predicted  segmentations  and their corresponding  
ground  truth annotations,  with values spanning  from 0 (indicating  com-
plete mismatch)  to 1 (representing  perfect alignment).  ASD provides  a 
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean

complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean 
distance  between  the surfaces  of predicted  and reference  structures,  
thereby  offering  sensitive  measurement  of contour  alignment  preci-
sion. DSC and ASD enable comprehensive  assessment  of both regional  
coverage  accuracy  and detailed  boundary  fidelity  in our segmentation  
results.
5.3. Comparison  with state-of-the-art  methods
The proposed  FAUDA-Net  is evaluated  against  eight state-of-the-art  
unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) methods:  (1) CycleGAN  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ) employs  cycle-consistent  generative  adversarial  networks  
to perform  unpaired  image-to-image  translation  between  domains,  (2)
SIFA (Chen et al., 2020a ) integrates  semantic-aware  image translation  
and feature alignment  in a unified  framework  to jointly adapt at pixel 
and feature levels, (3) DSAN (Han et al., 2021 ) introduces  a dual-
stream alignment  network  with domain-private  and shared components  
to reduce feature discrepancy  bidirectionally,  (4) SFDA (Bateson  et al., 
2022 ) formulates  a source-free  UDA strategy  that adapts models  via 
entropy  minimization  and class distribution  alignment  without  access-
ing source data, (5) SE-ASA  (Feng et al., 2023 ) employs  selective  
entropy  constraints  on confident  predictions  and adaptive  semantic  
alignment  to enhance  segmentation  consistency  across domains,  (6)
UNIT-DDPM  (Özbey et al., 2023 ) combines  denoising  diffusion  prob-
abilistic  models  with cycle-consistent  learning  to support  high-fidelity  
cross-domain  adaptation,  (7) SFS (Stan and Rostami , 2024 ) learns a 
domain-agnostic  feature representation  by projecting  both domains  
into a common  latent space with consistency  regularization,  and (8)
DDSP (Zheng et al., 2024 ) incorporates  semantic  preservation  into dis-

Unsupervised  domain adaptation  (UDA) has achieved  notable advances  in medical  image segmentation.  
However,  the significant  domain shifts between  source and target data continue  to pose fundamental  
challenges,  driving an urgent demand  for more robust cross-domain  solutions.  Current UDA methods  often 
rely on static spatial alignment  strategies  that ignore the dynamic  evolution  of feature distributions  during 
training,  often resulting  in blurred boundary  delineation  and loss of structural  details. To address these issues, 
we propose  a frequency-aware  unsupervised  domain adaptation  network  (FAUDA-Net),  which dynamically  
adapts to feature distribution  shifts and enhances  boundary  delineation  in the target domain.  Specifically,  
FAUDA-Net  introduces  dual-domain  distribution  disruption  to encourage  domain-invariant  representations,  
along with frequency  constraints,  that leverage  both phase and amplitude  components  to guide cross-domain  
adaptation.  Furthermore,  a frequency-aware  contrastive  learning  mechanism  aligns source and target features  
through  channel  self-attention  matrices,  enabling  a shared pixel-wise  decoder  to achieve robust segmentation

and PROMISE12,  demonstrate  that FAUDA-Net  outperforms  eight state-of-the-art  methods  in both overall 
segmentation  accuracy  (Dice) and boundary  extraction  precision  (ASD), providing  a reliable and effective  
solution  for multi-modal  and multi-center  medical  image segmentation.
1. Introduction
Deep neural networks  have significantly  advanced  medical  image 
segmentation  by leveraging  their powerful  feature extraction  capabil-
ities and effective  utilization  of annotated  datasets.  However,  these 
methods  typically  assume  that training  and testing data follow iden-
tical distribution  characteristics  and are often applied  within a single 
imaging  modality  (van Tulder and de Bruijne , 2018 ; Ouyang  et al., 
2022 ; Varoquaux  and Colliot , 2023 ). As shown in Fig.  1(a), real-
world medical  image analysis  scenarios  involve  significant  differences  
in contrast,  texture,  and intensity  between  modalities  such as MRI 
and CT, which challenges  this assumption.  These discrepancies  limit 
the generalization  capability  of conventional  models,  resulting  in sub-
optimal  performance  in cross-modal  applications.  In clinical  practice,  
utilizing  a model trained  on one modality  (e.g., MRI) to segment  images 
from another  modality  (e.g., CT) offers considerable  benefits:  it reduces  
annotation  costs and expands  the model’s  applicability.  Cross-modality  
(or cross-domain)  segmentation  capability  is clinically  significant,  as

As illustrated  in Fig.  1(b), unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) 
provides  an effective  solution  to mitigate  distribution  discrepancies  be-
tween source (training)  and target (testing)  data (Ganin and Lempitsky , 
2015 ; Hou et al., 2016 ; Cui et al., 2021 ; Liu et al., 2022 ). By em-
ploying  feature alignment  techniques,  UDA enables  models  to achieve  
segmentation  performance  on the target domain  comparable  to that 
on the source domain  without  requiring  annotations  for target data, 
significantly  reducing  labeling  costs and enhancing  the practicality  of 
deep learning  methods  in clinical  applications.  Developing  effective  
UDA methods  is thus critically  important  for cross-domain  medical  
image segmentation.  The primary  goal of UDA is to address  distribution  
shifts between  source and target domains,  which represents  a com-
mon challenge  in real-world  applications.  Early UDA methods  utilized  
generative  adversarial  networks  (GANs)  for pixel-level  style transfer,  
translating  source images into the style of the target domain  (Zhu et al.,

these limitations,  feature alignment  methods  were proposed  (Chen 
et al., 2020a ; Yeh et al., 2021 ; Shi et al., 2022 ), focusing  on minimizing  
statistical  distances  such as maximum  mean discrepancy  (Wang et al., 
2021 ) to align feature distributions  across domains.
The introduction  of adversarial  learning  based on feature align-
ment has significantly  advanced  domain  adaptation  through  the use 
of domain  classifiers  and adversarial  training  mechanisms  to align 
cross-domain  features,  thereby  enhancing  model generalization  (Zhang 
et al., 2022 ; Stan and Rostami , 2024 ; Lyu et al., 2025 ). However,  
these methods  remain challenged  by training  instability  and mode 
collapse,  especially  when dealing  with high-dimensional  and struc-
turally complex  medical  images.  More fundamentally,  most existing  
UDA approaches  rely on a static feature alignment  assumption  in the 
spatial domain,  ignoring  the dynamic  evolution  of feature distribu-
tions throughout  training.  As a result, they often fail to adequately  
model structural  details and boundary  regions  in the target domain.  
Furthermore,  conventional  UDA methods  often neglect  the important  
role of frequency-domain  information  in capturing  structural  semantics  
and cross-domain  distribution  differences,  which restricts  their ability 
to learn domain-invariant  features  effectively.  In fact, the phase and 
amplitude  components  of the frequency  domain  encode structural  in-
formation  and stylistic  variations,  respectively,  offering  rich cues for 
discriminative  and dynamic  domain  alignment.  Therefore,  developing  
an adaptive  framework  that can perceive  distribution  dynamics,  incor-

an adaptive  framework  that can perceive  distribution  dynamics,  incor-
porate frequency-domain  priors, and enhance  boundary  consistency  is 
crucial for improving  cross-domain  medical  image segmentation.
To tackle these issues, we propose  a frequency-aware  unsupervised  
domain  adaptation  network  (FAUDA-Net),  which enables  dynamic  dis-
tribution  adaptation  and refined  boundary-aware  segmentation.The main contributions  of this work are as follows:
•A dual-domain  distribution  perturbation  structure  that applies 
varying  degrees  of data perturbation  to source and target domain  
data, transforming  domain  distributions  from static to dynamic  
and promoting  domain-invariant  representation  learning.
•A bidirectional  frequency  domain  adaptation  (BFDA)  that ex-
plicitly decouples  structural  information  and style differences  
through  frequency-domain  constraints.  This strategy  utilizes
phase components  to maintain  cross-domain  structural  consis-
tency and leverages  amplitude  information  to guide style adapta-
tion,
thereby  enhancing  domain-invariant  feature representation  while 
reducing  cross-domain  distribution  discrepancies.
•A frequency-aware  contrastive  learning  (FACL)  mechanism  that 
employs  a contrastive  alignment  approach  based on frequency-
domain  priors. Through  channel  self-attention  matrices,  it models  
the correlation  between  source and target domain  features  in 
the frequency  domain.  This mechanism  enhances  feature discrim-
inability  using frequency  information  and effectively  mitigates  
the negative  impact of frequency  perturbations,  improving  the 
model’s  robustness  to target domain  features.
•Extensive  experiments  conducted  on three publicly  available  med-
ical image datasets,  MMWHS17,  BraTS21  and PROMISE12,
demonstrate  that FAUDA-Net  outperforms  eight state-of-the-art  
methods  in both overall segmentation  accuracy  (Dice) and bound-

methods  in both overall segmentation  accuracy  (Dice) and bound-
ary segmentation  quality (ASD), providing  an effective  and re-
liable solution  for cross-domain  medical  image segmentation  
tasks.
2. Related  works
In this section,  we review recent advances  closely related to our 
work. These approaches  can be roughly  categorized  into four cate-
gories: (1) image alignment  methods,  (2) simultaneous  feature and 
image alignment  methods,  (3) disentangled  representation  learning  
methods,  and (4) prior knowledge  constraint  methods.
2.1. Image alignment  methods
Image alignment  methods  aim to reduce the domain  gap by trans-
forming  source-domain  images to mimic the style of the target domain.  
A common  strategy  involves  using image-to-image  translation  net-
works, such as cycle-consistent  adversarial  networks  (CycleGAN)  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ), to generate  semantically  consistent  target-style  images 
from the source domain.  Similarly,  Huo et al. (2018 ) employed  a 
translation  network  to synthesize  images with target-domain  charac-
teristics  and used these generated  images along with their labels to 
train a segmentation  model. Zhang et al. (2019 ) introduced  content  and 
style discriminators  to preserve  structural  semantics  and enforce  noise 
patterns  consistent  with the target domain,  respectively.  However,  
these methods  often suffer from semantic  distortions  and artifacts  in 
the translated  images,  limiting  their effectiveness.
Furthermore,  Henry et al. (2021 ) improved  semantic  preservation  
through  conditional  GANs and L1 loss, yet required  paired data, which 
restricts  its scalability.  Other style transfer  methods  such as AdaIN (Gu 
and Ye, 2021 ) adapted  feature statistics  to align styles but were highly

2.2. Simultaneous  feature and image alignment  methods
Considering  that the advantages  of image alignment  and feature 
alignment  can be leveraged  to tackle domain  adaptation  problems,  
many recent studies adopt both strategies  concurrently.  For exam-
ple, Chen et al. (2020a ) introduced  SIFA, a novel framework  for cross-
modal medical  image segmentation  that effectively  fuses image and 
feature alignment.  Han et al. (2021 ) proposed  DSAN, a symmetric  adap-
tation network  designed  to achieve  bidirectional  alignment  between  
source and target domain  translation  sub-networks.  Moreover,  Ji and 
Chung (2023 ) developed  MA-UDA,  a transformer-based  approach  that 
incorporates  meta-attention  to enable a comprehensive  attention-based  
alignment  mechanism  at the feature level, in addition  to employing  
GANs for image-level  alignment.  Feng et al. (2023 ) proposed  an adap-
tive semantic  alignment  module  that reduces  inter-domain  discrepancy  
at the class level by aligning  prototype  representations  across do-
mains, where unreliable  pixels are filtered  out to obtain more robust 
and accurate  feature prototypes.  Additionally,  Jiang et al. (2024 ) pre-
sented a multi-feature  joint discriminative  domain  adaptation  method  
that simultaneously  leverages  both feature alignment  and edge align-
ment to enhance  unsupervised  domain  adaptation  for femur X-ray 
image segmentation.  Extending  this concept  to the detection  task, Li 
et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework

et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework  
that integrates  feature and image alignment  with adversarial  learning  
to improve  the robustness  of multi-center  bone tumor detection  on 
radiographs.
2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.
2.4. Prior knowledge  constraint  methods
Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-

source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-
tropy over target data while incorporating  anatomical  priors via KL 
divergence.  This method  effectively  handles  scenarios  where source 
images are unavailable  due to privacy  constraints.  Diao et al. (2024 ) 
developed  TSANet,  a two-stage  pipeline  combining  Fourier-based  style 
transfer  with anatomical  entropy  minimization.  While improving  seg-
mentation  accuracy,  its adaptability  is limited  in domains  with sig-
nificant  structural  variations.  Gupta et al. (2022 ) incorporated  topo-
logical constraints  to enforce  geometric  relationships  between  organs,  
though  its reliance  on annotated  data to identify  and refine critical 
pixels restricts  its application  in fully unsupervised  settings.  Kervadec  et al. (2019 ) designed  a volume-based  regularization  term for weakly-
supervised  segmentation,  while Zhou et al. (2019 ) used statistical  label 
distributions  with KL divergence  guidance.  Zheng et al. (2024 ) pro-
posed DDSP, which builds upon feature disentanglement  with semantic  
consistency  and domain  perturbation  to improve  pseudo-label  quality.  
However,  these methods  generally  require  dataset-specific  pre-analysis  
or explicit  anatomical  constraints,  limiting  their flexibility  in handling  
dynamic  domain  shifts.
In contrast,  our FAUDA-Net  introduces  a frequency-aware  con-
trastive  alignment  mechanism  that captures  both structural  consistency  
and stylistic  variance  through  adaptive  frequency-domain  learning.  Un-
like methods  that depend  on pre-defined  spatial constraints  or dataset-
specific  statistical  priors, our approach  leverages  phase and amplitude  
representations  to achieve  non-rigid  and dynamic  feature alignment  
across domains.  By integrating  frequency-domain  cues with contrastive  
learning,  FAUDA-Net  aligns features  without  requiring  annotated  data 
in the target domain  or pre-computed  constraints,  enabling  robust

adaptation  is performed  by alternating  MRI and CT as source domains.

251 cases allocated  for validation  and testing.  All volumes  are pre-

U-Net as the encoder,  with the channel  configuration  for each layer set

the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder  
network.  The frequency  mixing ratio parameter  𝛽 was configured  as

per_question_results.question: 在医学图像分割领域，哪些方法利用了频率域信息？
per_question_results.ground_truth: 医学图像分割领域利用频率域信息的方法包括：FAUDA-Net（频率感知对比学习）、Ge 等人的方法（FFT 风格适应 + 相位谱边界增强）、APEX（傅里叶频谱提取域特征）、腹腔镜图像域适应（径向频率掩码 + Fourier Domain Adaptation-Blend）、以及 FADA（Haar 小波变换解耦内容和风格）。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问～😊

在医学图像分割领域，根据知识库内容，目前明确利用频率域信息的方法主要是本文提出的 **FAUDA-Net（Frequency-aware Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Network）**。该方法系统性地引入并融合了频率域的相位（phase）和幅度（amplitude）信息，用于解决跨域分割中的分布偏移、结构不一致与边界模糊等问题。具体包括以下三方面频率域技术：

1. **双向频率域适应（BFDA）**：通过傅里叶变换（FFT）显式解耦结构信息（由相位谱编码）和风格差异（由幅度谱编码），分别施加相位谱一致性（PSC）和幅度谱一致性（ASC）约束，从而增强跨域解剖结构保持能力【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】。

2. **频率感知对比学习（FACL）**：基于频率域先验构建通道自注意力矩阵，在频域中对齐源域与目标域特征，提升类内紧凑性与类间可分性，并缓解频率扰动带来的负面影响【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】。

3. **频域扰动生成负样本**：在BFDA模块中，通过将增强后源域的幅度谱与目标域的相位谱组合，生成频域扰动图像（如公式11所示），为对比学习提供合成负样本【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】。

此外，知识库中还提到其他方法虽未直接建模频率域，但存在相关尝试：  
- TSANet采用了**基于傅里叶的风格迁移（Fourier-based style transfer）**，用于跨域风格适配【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】；  
- 一些传统UDA方法被指出“忽视了频率域信息在捕获结构语义和跨域分布差异中的重要作用”，反向印证了频率域信息的价值【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】。

需要说明的是，知识库中未提及其他明确使用频率域信息的医学图像分割方法（如传统滤波、小波变换或频域正则化等）。若您想了解某类特定方法（如基于小波/多尺度频域建模）是否适用，或需技术细节解读（如PSC/ASC实现原理），欢迎随时告诉我，我可为您进一步梳理～  

如您有实际应用需求（如模型部署、参数调优或数据适配问题），也建议转接人工技术客服，他们可为您提供一对一支持哦！🌟

In this section,  we review recent advances  closely related to our 
work. These approaches  can be roughly  categorized  into four cate-

image alignment  methods,  (3) disentangled  representation  learning  
methods,  and (4) prior knowledge  constraint  methods.
2.1. Image alignment  methods
Image alignment  methods  aim to reduce the domain  gap by trans-
forming  source-domain  images to mimic the style of the target domain.  
A common  strategy  involves  using image-to-image  translation  net-

2.2. Simultaneous  feature and image alignment  methods
Considering  that the advantages  of image alignment  and feature 
alignment  can be leveraged  to tackle domain  adaptation  problems,  
many recent studies adopt both strategies  concurrently.  For exam-
ple, Chen et al. (2020a ) introduced  SIFA, a novel framework  for cross-
modal medical  image segmentation  that effectively  fuses image and 
feature alignment.  Han et al. (2021 ) proposed  DSAN, a symmetric  adap-
tation network  designed  to achieve  bidirectional  alignment  between  
source and target domain  translation  sub-networks.  Moreover,  Ji and 
Chung (2023 ) developed  MA-UDA,  a transformer-based  approach  that 
incorporates  meta-attention  to enable a comprehensive  attention-based  
alignment  mechanism  at the feature level, in addition  to employing  
GANs for image-level  alignment.  Feng et al. (2023 ) proposed  an adap-
tive semantic  alignment  module  that reduces  inter-domain  discrepancy  
at the class level by aligning  prototype  representations  across do-
mains, where unreliable  pixels are filtered  out to obtain more robust 
and accurate  feature prototypes.  Additionally,  Jiang et al. (2024 ) pre-
sented a multi-feature  joint discriminative  domain  adaptation  method  
that simultaneously  leverages  both feature alignment  and edge align-
ment to enhance  unsupervised  domain  adaptation  for femur X-ray 
image segmentation.  Extending  this concept  to the detection  task, Li 
et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework

2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.
2.4. Prior knowledge  constraint  methods
Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-

tropy over target data while incorporating  anatomical  priors via KL 
divergence.  This method  effectively  handles  scenarios  where source 
images are unavailable  due to privacy  constraints.  Diao et al. (2024 ) 
developed  TSANet,  a two-stage  pipeline  combining  Fourier-based  style 
transfer  with anatomical  entropy  minimization.  While improving  seg-
mentation  accuracy,  its adaptability  is limited  in domains  with sig-
nificant  structural  variations.  Gupta et al. (2022 ) incorporated  topo-
logical constraints  to enforce  geometric  relationships  between  organs,  
though  its reliance  on annotated  data to identify  and refine critical 
pixels restricts  its application  in fully unsupervised  settings.  Kervadec  et al. (2019 ) designed  a volume-based  regularization  term for weakly-
supervised  segmentation,  while Zhou et al. (2019 ) used statistical  label 
distributions  with KL divergence  guidance.  Zheng et al. (2024 ) pro-
posed DDSP, which builds upon feature disentanglement  with semantic  
consistency  and domain  perturbation  to improve  pseudo-label  quality.  
However,  these methods  generally  require  dataset-specific  pre-analysis  
or explicit  anatomical  constraints,  limiting  their flexibility  in handling  
dynamic  domain  shifts.
In contrast,  our FAUDA-Net  introduces  a frequency-aware  con-
trastive  alignment  mechanism  that captures  both structural  consistency  
and stylistic  variance  through  adaptive  frequency-domain  learning.  Un-
like methods  that depend  on pre-defined  spatial constraints  or dataset-
specific  statistical  priors, our approach  leverages  phase and amplitude  
representations  to achieve  non-rigid  and dynamic  feature alignment  
across domains.  By integrating  frequency-domain  cues with contrastive  
learning,  FAUDA-Net  aligns features  without  requiring  annotated  data 
in the target domain  or pre-computed  constraints,  enabling  robust

5.1. Datasets
To comprehensively  evaluate  the performance  of our proposed  
method,  we conduct  experiments  on three publicly  available  medical  
image segmentation  datasets:  MMWHS17  (Gao et al., 2023 ) for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation,  BraTS21  (Han et al., 2021 ) 
for cross-sequence  brain glioma segmentation,  and PROMISE12  (Liu 
et al., 2020 ) for cross-site  prostate  segmentation.
(1) MMWHS17  Dataset:  The Multi-Modality  Whole Heart Segmen-
tation Challenge  2017 (MMWHS17)  dataset  is employed  for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation.  The dataset  contains  20 
MRI and 20 CT scans with corresponding  voxel-wise  annotations.  Fol-
lowing the experimental  setup in Zheng et al. (2024 ), we focus on four 
cardiac  structures:  ascending  aorta (AA), left atrium blood cavity (LAC), 
left ventricle  blood cavity (LVC), and left ventricle  myocardium  (MYO).  
We employ  a two-fold  cross-validation  strategy,  with 20 source domain  
scans and 10 target domain  scans for training,  and the remaining  10 
target scans for testing.  All scans are reoriented  to RAI orientation,  
cropped  to 128 × 128 × 128 voxels, and intensity-normalized  (CT: -
100 to 800 HU; MRI: 0.5th to 99.5th percentiles).  Bidirectional  domain  
adaptation  is performed  by alternating  MRI and CT as source domains.
(2) BraTS21  Dataset:  The BraTS21  Dataset  comprises  1251 MRI 
scans, each including  four modality  sequences  (T1, T1ce, T2, and 
FLAIR) and annotated  with tumor sub-regions.  To address  the distinct  
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences

tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences  
are chosen for bidirectional  domain  adaptation,  focusing  on the seg-
mentation  of the whole tumor region. The dataset  is partitioned  into 
500 scans per domain  for source and target training,  with an additional  
251 cases allocated  for validation  and testing.  All volumes  are pre-
processed  via brain-region  centering  and cropped  to a consistent  size of 
128 × 128 × 128. Intensity  values are normalized  based on the 0.5th 
to 99.5th percentile  range to reduce scanner-specific  variations.  This 
setup enables  a focused  evaluation  of domain  adaptation  under pro-
nounced  inter-modality  distribution  shifts, particularly  in the context  
of structural  and contrast  differences  between  T2 and FLAIR imaging.
(3) PROMISE12  Dataset:  The PROMISE12  challenge  dataset  is used 
for cross-site  prostate  segmentation,  comprising  T2-weighted  MRI scans

from each site. We randomly  split the 12 target scans into two folds 
and perform  two-fold  cross-validation.  For preprocessing,  we manually  
crop the original  scans to focus on the prostate  region and resize all

RTX 3090 GPU with 24 GB memory.  The model was implemented  in 
PyTorch  and optimized  using the Adam optimizer.  We adopted  a 3D 
U-Net as the encoder,  with the channel  configuration  for each layer set

ResNet blocks and a convolutional  layer, where the output channels  
match the number  of classes.  To balance  training  stability  and adap-
tation efficiency,  we applied  differentiated  learning  rates: 1 × 10−4 for 
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder

per_question_results.question: FARL 和 APEX 都使用了提示学习，它们的区别是什么？
per_question_results.ground_truth: FARL 是用于视觉-语言模型（VLM）少样本泛化的框架，通过傅里叶分析解耦结构和风格特征，使用双交叉注意力机制生成解耦的表示 token。APEX 是用于医学图像分割的自适应视觉提示框架，通过傅里叶频谱提取域特征来查询可学习的提示记忆库。FARL 面向 VLM 的少样本学习，APEX 面向医学图像分割的域泛化。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问，很高兴为您解答关于FARL和APEX的区别问题。作为专业客服，我已严格依据您提供的知识库内容进行梳理，以下是二者的核心区别：

1. **核心目标与应用场景不同**  
   - FARL（Fourier-Attentive Representation Learning）聚焦于**视觉-语言模型（VLM）的少样本适应**，尤其面向**图像分类任务**（如ImageNet、EuroSAT、DTD等15个数据集），旨在提升模型在**基类（base）与新类（novel）之间的泛化能力**及**跨域鲁棒性**（如ImageNet→ImageNet-V2/Sketch/A/R）【来源：《2512.04395v2.pdf》】。  
   - APEX（Adaptive Prompt EXtraction）专为**医学图像分割任务**设计，解决临床中因设备/扫描参数差异导致的**域偏移问题**（如结肠息肉、视杯视盘OC/OD分割），强调对**同一解剖结构在不同成像域下的自适应提示生成**【来源：《2604.17455v1.pdf》】。

2. **提示机制的设计逻辑不同**  
   - FARL采用**频域显式解耦+不对称注入**：将输入图像通过FFT分解为**相位（结构）与幅度（风格）分量**，分别建模为“Geometry Expert”和“Context Expert”，再通过交叉注意力动态融合；其提示（representation tokens）被**不对称地注入文本编码器（增强语义对齐）和图像编码器（作为正则化锚点）**【来源：《2512.04395v2.pdf》】。  
   - APEX采用**低频特征驱动的记忆检索**：从图像的**低频幅度谱**中提取域判别特征，再通过可学习的**提示记忆库（Prompt Memory, J=150 slots）** 自适应检索**输入级（input-specific）提示**，而非统一域级提示；提示仅作用于**低频分量**，以保留高频解剖结构完整性【来源：《2604.17455v1.pdf》】。

3. **技术实现关键差异**  
   - FARL依赖**傅里叶变换与双流注意力架构**，强调**表示层解耦**（representation-level disentanglement），避免传统数据增强式频域操作【来源：《2512.04395v2.pdf》】。  
   - APEX引入**低频特征对比学习（LFC loss）**，通过拉近同域/推远异域的低频特征，提升记忆库中提示的域区分能力；其计算开销极小（仅0.036M参数，+20ms推理耗时），适合临床实时场景【来源：《2604.17455v1.pdf》】。

简言之：FARL是面向通用视觉-语言模型的**频域结构化提示学习框架**，重在**解耦几何与风格以提升少样本泛化**；而APEX是面向医学分割的**自适应记忆式提示框架**，重在**基于低频域特征动态检索输入专属提示以应对设备差异**。

如您需要进一步了解某项技术细节（例如FARL的相位注意力可视化或APEX在Drishti-GS数据集上的具体指标），欢迎随时告诉我，我将为您精准定位知识库内容！😊

5. Conclusion
In this work, we introduced APEX, an adaptive visual
prompting framework designed to improve the general-
izability of prompt-based domain adaptation in medical
image segmentation. Unlike existing methods that ap-
ply a single prompt uniformly across a domain, APEX
adaptively generates input-specific prompts by leveraging
a learned memory of domain-discriminative features. To
further enhance domain-level feature discrimination, we
proposed an LFC learning framework that encourages ro-
bust intra-domain clustering and inter-domain discrimina-
tion. Extensive experiments on two medical segmentation
tasks demonstrated that APEX consistently outperforms
SOTA prompting methods on both seen and unseen do-
mains. These results highlight the potential of input-aware,

2.2. Visual Prompting for Domain Adaptation
Prompt learning was initially designed to provide additional
text context for the input text to tune the Natural Language
Processing (NLP) models or multi-modal models [17, 29].
After the success in NLP task, it is deployed in vision tasks.
For the vision task, user-defined interactive VPs also pro-
vide additional context to the vision models as bounding
box, points, etc [19, 24, 45].
Different from user-defined prompts, learnable VPs can
also be used for domain adaptation [6, 22, 23, 43, 49]. By
optimizing learnable parameters added to input images, it
projects input data to a new space and makes the input
perform well on the pre-trained model. Since it does not
change the parameters of the pre-trained model, it preserves
source-domain knowledge and mitigates catastrophic for-
getting, while avoiding direct access to source data. Thus,
it can successfully adapt target domain data to pre-trained
models. Early work by Jiaet al.[22] introduced VPs to
adapt vision transformers. Meta-Padding [23] extended this
idea by inserting learnable padding tokens at the input and
feature levels. FVP [43] embedded prompts in the Fourier

6 Conclusion
We revisited few-shot VLM adaptation through a spectral lens and identified
spectral bias, the tendency to overfit domain-specific amplitude statistics, as
a key obstacle to generalization. To address this issue, we proposedFARL, a
framework that enforces representation-level spectral disentanglement beyond
holistic feature tuning.
By explicitly separating phase-derived structure and amplitude-derived style
and integrating them via an asymmetric injection strategy, FARL encourages
models to prioritize robust geometric cues while retaining useful contextual in-
formation. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved robustness in base-to-
novel generalization and cross-dataset transfer.
More broadly, our results suggest that integrating fundamental signal pro-
cessing principles directly into the representation learning loop, rather than us-
ing them solely for data augmentation, offers a promising direction for few-shot
vision-language adaptation.

1 Introduction
Vision-Language Models (VLMs), such as CLIP [20], have shown remarkable
zero-shot and few-shot transfer capabilities by aligning images and text in a
shared embedding space. To adapt these foundation models efficiently, recent
work has focused on prompt learning [34,35] and adapter-based strategies [6,
11,28,31], which freeze the backbone and optimize lightweight learnable compo-

We argue that this fragility stems not merely from limited capacity, but
from a fundamentalspectral biasin few-shot adaptation. It is well known
that neural networks tend to rely on superficial statistics such as texture and
color before learning robust semantic structure [5]. From a Fourier perspective,
these superficial cues are primarily encoded in the amplitude spectrum, whilearXiv:2512.04395v2  [cs.CV]  28 Feb 2026

spectral components are implicitly entangled, causing few-shot learners to over-

This exposes a gap in current approaches. Prompt learning methods treat
visual representations as black boxes, offering no control over which spectral
components drive adaptation. Meanwhile, Fourier-based techniques explored in
domain generalization [27,29] primarily use spectral manipulation as a data
augmentation strategy, rather than as an explicit mechanism for representation
learning within VLMs.

ing (FARL), a framework that explicitly mitigates spectral bias during VLM

strategy, enabling the model to align structure-centric visual features with se-
mantically adaptive textual prompts while preserving robust visual representa-
tions.

per_question_results.ground_truth: AFNO（Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator）在频率域进行全局 token 混合，避免了传统多头自注意力的 O(N^2) 注意力权重计算，实现了准线性计算复杂度和线性内存扩展，同时保留了全局上下文建模能力。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问，很高兴为您解答关于AMBER-AFNO中AFNO技术优势的问题。根据知识库内容，AFNO（Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators）相比传统多头自注意力（MHSA）具有以下明确优势：

1. **计算复杂度显著降低**：传统自注意力机制具有O(N²)的二次复杂度，内存和计算开销随输入尺寸平方增长；而AFNO通过在频域进行全局token混合，实现准线性（quasi-linear）计算复杂度和线性内存使用，有效缓解3D医学图像分割中的计算瓶颈【来源：《2508.01941v2.pdf》】。

2. **参数量大幅减少**：AMBER-AFNO在ACDC数据集上仅需14.77M参数，比UNETR++（66.8M）少约78%，同时Dice分数更高（92.85% vs. 92.83%）；相比MHSA版AMBER（19.01M），AFNO版本（14.77M或轻量版8.70M）参数更少且性能更强【来源：《2508.01941v2.pdf》】。

3. **避免token-to-token交互，提升效率与可扩展性**：AFNO不构建N²规模的注意力矩阵，而是通过3D快速傅里叶变换（RFFT）、可学习复数MLP频域滤波及软阈值处理，在频域完成全局混合，从而消除逐对token计算，更适合高分辨率3D体数据【来源：《2508.01941v2.pdf》】。

4. **保持甚至提升分割精度**：在ACDC、Synapse和BraTS三大基准上，AMBER-AFNO均达到SOTA或近SOTA Dice分数（如ACDC达92.85%，BraTS达82.82%），且在最具挑战性的Enhancing Tumor子区域（ET）上取得最高Dice（80.33%），证明其频域建模能力不逊于甚至优于传统注意力【来源：《2508.01941v2.pdf》】。

5. **架构更简洁、部署更友好**：无需解码器分支、多尺度融合层级或深层注意力堆叠，模型模块化强，易于跨数据集迁移，且GPU显存占用极低（仅2.96GB），支持在中端显卡（如NVIDIA L40）上实现<100ms推理延迟【来源：《2508.01941v2.pdf》】。

We adapt the remote sensing-inspired AMBER model (Dosi et al., 2025) from multi-band image
segmentation to 3D medical datacube segmentation. To address the computational bottleneck of the
volumetric transformer, we propose the AMBER-AFNO architecture. This approach uses Adaptive
FourierNeuralOperators(AFNO)insteadofthemulti-headself-attentionmechanism.Unlikespatial
pairwise interactions between tokens, global token mixing in the frequency domain avoids(𝑁2)
attention-weightcalculations.Asaresult,AMBER-AFNOachievesquasi-linearcomputationalcom-
plexity and linear memory scaling.
This new way to model global context reduces reliance on dense transformers while preserving
global contextual modeling capability. By using attention-free spectral operations, our design offers
a compact parameterization and maintains a competitive computational complexity. We evaluate
AMBER-AFNO on three public datasets: ACDC, Synapse, and BraTS. On these datasets, the
model achieves state-of-the-art or near-state-of-the-art results for DSC and HD95. Compared with
recent compact CNN and Transformer architectures, our approach yields higher Dice scores while
maintaining a compact model size.

To explicitly address the efficiency–globality trade-off in
3D lightweight medical image segmentation, we propose
AMBER-AFNO, where Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators
(AFNO) (Guibas et al., 2021) replace multi-head self-
attention within a hierarchical transformer encoder. Instead
of constructing quadratic attention matrices, AFNO per-
formsglobaltokenmixinginthefrequencydomainthrough
learnable spectral filters, enabling quasi-linear computa-
tional complexity and linear memory cost. The multi-head
structuraldesignispreservedthroughblock-wisefrequency
mixing, allowing different frequency subspaces to capture
distinct semantic patterns without pairwise token interac-
tions. In contrast to attention approximation strategies or
convolution–attention compression schemes, this approach
reformulates global context modeling itself rather than
merely reducing attention computation.
BuildingontheAMBERarchitecture,theproposedAMBER-
AFNO adapts spectral-domain token mixing to full 3D
volumetricsegmentation.Thisdesignreducestheparameter
count by nearly 78% compared with heavy transformer-
based models such as UNETR++, while maintaining com-
petitive FLOPs and segmentation performance. Unlike re-
centlightweightCNN–Transformervariants(e.g.,LW-CTrans
(Kuang et al., 2025)), whose efficiency is achieved by sim-
plifyingconvolutionalorattentionmodules,thelightweight
property of AMBER-AFNO stems from spectral-domain
global mixing.
We validate AMBER-AFNO on three public 3D medical
segmentation benchmarks: ACDC (Bernard et al., 2018),
Synapse (Landman et al., 2015), and BraTS (Menze et al.,
2015). Using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Haus-
dorffDistance(HD95)asevaluationmetrics,theexperimen-
tal results demonstrate that spectral-domain token mixing
achieves a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off across
diverse anatomical scenarios.

modeling global context. We do this by removing token-
to-token interactions and ensuring tokens are mixed in the
spectral domain. Our design delivers quasi-linear complex-
ity and linear memory growth with respect to volume size.

detailed tumour structure.

than 3% increase in segmentation accuracy with a small
number of parameters. This implies that frequency-domain
token mixing works well for multimodal and multi-region
segmentationtasks,furthervalidatingthegeneralizabilityof
theproposedframeworkacrossvariousclinicalapplications.

3.2. Lightweight All-MLP Decoder
The four feature maps produced by the MiT encoder are
first channel-projected to a common embedding size𝑑by
position-agnostic MLP layers. Then every projected tensor
is trilinearly upsampled to the finest encoder resolution and
concatenated along the channel axis. A1 × 1 × 1convo-
lution with RELU activation and 3-D batch normalization
fuses this aggregate into a compact representation. A single
transposed3-Dconvolutionsubsequentlydoublesthespatial
dimensions, bringing the volume back to the native voxel
grid while reducing the channels to𝑁cls. A final1 × 1 × 1
convolution sharpens the logits, yielding the segmentation
mask𝑀∈ℝ𝑁cls×𝐷×𝐻×𝑊. Compared with the original
five-stageAMBERdecoder,thisvariantomitsthededicated
spectral-reduction block and integrates the final MLP into
the transposed convolution, lowering memory cost without
sacrificing accuracy.

Transformer-based and efficient attention models.
Global self-attention in Vision Transformers has proven ef-
fective for representation learning. In volumetric segmenta-
tion,UNETR(Hatamizadehetal.,2021)andSwin-UNETR
(Hatamizadeh et al., 2022) demonstrate the importance of
hierarchicaltokeninteractions.nnFormer(Zhouetal.,2023)

(Shaker et al., 2024) proposed Efficient Paired Attention
(EPA) for separating spatial and channel attention. DS-
UNETR++ (Jiang et al., 2025) further introduced gated
cross-attention mechanisms.
In its standard form, self-attention grows quadratically with
the number of tokens, making it costly for larger 3D inputs.
Linformer(Wangetal.,2020)andPerformer(Choromanski
et al., 2022) apply low-rank and kernel-based approxima-
tions,whileFNet(Lee-Thorpetal.,2022)replacesattention
with fixed Fourier transforms.
In contrast, Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators (AFNO)
(Guibas et al., 2021) learn frequency filters and block di-
agonal channel mixing matrices for token mixing in the
Fourier domain. By truncating high-frequency modes and
applying adaptive frequency filters, AFNO achieves quasi-
linear complexity and linear memory cost while modeling
globalcontext.AFNOwasoriginallyproposedfor3-channel
images, and its potential for volumetric medical segmenta-
tion remains underexplored.

per_question_results.question: SFD-ADNet 为什么使用双向 Mamba 而不是传统 Transformer？
per_question_results.ground_truth: SFD-ADNet 使用双向 Mamba 变形预测器来捕获长程几何依赖和局部结构变化，实现自适应的位置感知变形控制。Mamba 相比传统 Transformer 在处理长序列时具有线性复杂度优势，更适合点云这种无序且可能很长的数据结构。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问，很高兴为您解答关于SFD-ADNet技术设计的问题。

SFD-ADNet选择使用双向Mamba而非传统Transformer，主要基于以下三点原因，均源自论文原文：

1. **计算效率优势：Mamba具有线性复杂度，而Transformer为二次复杂度**  
   论文明确指出：“Mamba采用状态空间建模范式，具有线性复杂度，能够高效建模长程依赖，同时保持局部几何保真度；相比之下，基于Transformer的模型因二次计算复杂度，在处理长点云序列时受限，常需粗粒度分块，可能导致细粒度几何细节丢失”【来源：《jimaging-12-00058-v2.pdf》】。

2. **更适配频谱特征建模需求**  
   在频谱域建模中，需处理“扩展频率序列”，而双向Mamba的双向设计可“同时编码全局结构趋势与局部高频变化”，这与点云频谱特征的特性高度匹配【来源：《jimaging-12-00058-v2.pdf》】。

3. **稳定建模长程依赖，缓解无序点云的伪序列依赖问题**  
   论文在3.1.2节指出：“为缓解无序点云易产生的伪序列依赖问题，采用双向Mamba替代自注意力机制来建模频谱特征依赖”【来源：《jimaging-12-00058-v2.pdf》】；并强调其“能稳定、可扩展地建模长程依赖”，这对点云全局上下文与局部结构联合建模至关重要【来源：《jimaging-12-00058-v2.pdf》】。

Abstract
Existing 3D point cloud enhancement methods typically rely on artificially designed geo-
metric transformations or local blending strategies, which are prone to introducing illogical
deformations, struggle to preserve global structure, and exhibit insufficient adaptability
to diverse degradation patterns. To address these limitations, this paper proposes SFD-
ADNet—an adaptive deformation framework based on a dual spatial–frequency domain.
It achieves 3D point cloud augmentation by explicitly learning deformation parameters
rather than applying predefined perturbations. By jointly modeling spatial structural de-
pendencies and spectral features, SFD-ADNet generates augmented samples that are both
structurally aware and task-relevant. In the spatial domain, a hierarchical sequence encoder
coupled with a bidirectional Mamba-based deformation predictor captures long-range
geometric dependencies and local structural variations, enabling adaptive position-aware
deformation control. In the frequency domain, a multi-scale dual-channel mechanism based
on adaptive Chebyshev polynomials separates low-frequency structural components from
high-frequency details, allowing the model to suppress noise-sensitive distortions while

local point deletion (D-L: 61.3%), SFD-ADNet’s error performance significantly outper-
formed PointWOLF [ 58], Wolfmix [ 57], and other enhancement strategies. Under rotational

per_question_results.question: 在域适应方法中，低频和高频分量通常分别代表什么信息？
per_question_results.ground_truth: 在域适应和图像处理中，低频分量通常代表场景内容和结构信息（域不变的），而高频分量通常代表风格、纹理和细节信息（域特定的）。例如，FADA 中低频分支稳定场景内容，高频分支学习场景风格；SFD-ADNet 中低频代表结构分量，高频代表细节。

of harnessing the Haar wavelet transform for DGSS, which can also inspire advancements in general
visual domain generalization.

6 Conclusion
In this paper, we focused on adapting VFM for DGSS by exploiting the style-invariant properties
from the VFMs, and presented a novel Frequency- ADA pted learning scheme to push this frontier.
Concisely, Haar wavelet transform was introduced to decouple the frozen VFM features into low- and

Unsupervised  domain adaptation  (UDA) has achieved  notable advances  in medical  image segmentation.  
However,  the significant  domain shifts between  source and target data continue  to pose fundamental  
challenges,  driving an urgent demand  for more robust cross-domain  solutions.  Current UDA methods  often 
rely on static spatial alignment  strategies  that ignore the dynamic  evolution  of feature distributions  during 
training,  often resulting  in blurred boundary  delineation  and loss of structural  details. To address these issues, 
we propose  a frequency-aware  unsupervised  domain adaptation  network  (FAUDA-Net),  which dynamically  
adapts to feature distribution  shifts and enhances  boundary  delineation  in the target domain.  Specifically,  
FAUDA-Net  introduces  dual-domain  distribution  disruption  to encourage  domain-invariant  representations,  
along with frequency  constraints,  that leverage  both phase and amplitude  components  to guide cross-domain  
adaptation.  Furthermore,  a frequency-aware  contrastive  learning  mechanism  aligns source and target features  
through  channel  self-attention  matrices,  enabling  a shared pixel-wise  decoder  to achieve robust segmentation

through  channel  self-attention  matrices,  enabling  a shared pixel-wise  decoder  to achieve robust segmentation  
performance.  Extensive  experiments  on three representative  medical  image datasets,  MMWHS17,  BraTS21,

1. Introduction
Deep neural networks  have significantly  advanced  medical  image 
segmentation  by leveraging  their powerful  feature extraction  capabil-
ities and effective  utilization  of annotated  datasets.  However,  these 
methods  typically  assume  that training  and testing data follow iden-
tical distribution  characteristics  and are often applied  within a single 
imaging  modality  (van Tulder and de Bruijne , 2018 ; Ouyang  et al., 
2022 ; Varoquaux  and Colliot , 2023 ). As shown in Fig.  1(a), real-
world medical  image analysis  scenarios  involve  significant  differences  
in contrast,  texture,  and intensity  between  modalities  such as MRI 
and CT, which challenges  this assumption.  These discrepancies  limit 
the generalization  capability  of conventional  models,  resulting  in sub-
optimal  performance  in cross-modal  applications.  In clinical  practice,  
utilizing  a model trained  on one modality  (e.g., MRI) to segment  images 
from another  modality  (e.g., CT) offers considerable  benefits:  it reduces  
annotation  costs and expands  the model’s  applicability.  Cross-modality  
(or cross-domain)  segmentation  capability  is clinically  significant,  as

As illustrated  in Fig.  1(b), unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) 
provides  an effective  solution  to mitigate  distribution  discrepancies  be-
tween source (training)  and target (testing)  data (Ganin and Lempitsky , 
2015 ; Hou et al., 2016 ; Cui et al., 2021 ; Liu et al., 2022 ). By em-

segmentation  performance  on the target domain  comparable  to that 
on the source domain  without  requiring  annotations  for target data, 
significantly  reducing  labeling  costs and enhancing  the practicality  of 
deep learning  methods  in clinical  applications.  Developing  effective  
UDA methods  is thus critically  important  for cross-domain  medical  
image segmentation.  The primary  goal of UDA is to address  distribution  
shifts between  source and target domains,  which represents  a com-
mon challenge  in real-world  applications.  Early UDA methods  utilized  
generative  adversarial  networks  (GANs)  for pixel-level  style transfer,  
translating  source images into the style of the target domain  (Zhu et al.,

The introduction  of adversarial  learning  based on feature align-
ment has significantly  advanced  domain  adaptation  through  the use 
of domain  classifiers  and adversarial  training  mechanisms  to align 
cross-domain  features,  thereby  enhancing  model generalization  (Zhang

these methods  remain challenged  by training  instability  and mode

spatial domain,  ignoring  the dynamic  evolution  of feature distribu-

model structural  details and boundary  regions  in the target domain.

amplitude  components  of the frequency  domain  encode structural  in-
formation  and stylistic  variations,  respectively,  offering  rich cues for 
discriminative  and dynamic  domain  alignment.  Therefore,  developing  
an adaptive  framework  that can perceive  distribution  dynamics,  incor-

2. Related  works
In this section,  we review recent advances  closely related to our 
work. These approaches  can be roughly  categorized  into four cate-
gories: (1) image alignment  methods,  (2) simultaneous  feature and 
image alignment  methods,  (3) disentangled  representation  learning  
methods,  and (4) prior knowledge  constraint  methods.
2.1. Image alignment  methods
Image alignment  methods  aim to reduce the domain  gap by trans-
forming  source-domain  images to mimic the style of the target domain.  
A common  strategy  involves  using image-to-image  translation  net-
works, such as cycle-consistent  adversarial  networks  (CycleGAN)  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ), to generate  semantically  consistent  target-style  images 
from the source domain.  Similarly,  Huo et al. (2018 ) employed  a 
translation  network  to synthesize  images with target-domain  charac-
teristics  and used these generated  images along with their labels to 
train a segmentation  model. Zhang et al. (2019 ) introduced  content  and 
style discriminators  to preserve  structural  semantics  and enforce  noise 
patterns  consistent  with the target domain,  respectively.  However,  
these methods  often suffer from semantic  distortions  and artifacts  in 
the translated  images,  limiting  their effectiveness.
Furthermore,  Henry et al. (2021 ) improved  semantic  preservation  
through  conditional  GANs and L1 loss, yet required  paired data, which 
restricts  its scalability.  Other style transfer  methods  such as AdaIN (Gu 
and Ye, 2021 ) adapted  feature statistics  to align styles but were highly 
sensitive  to hyperparameter  settings.  Recently,  ISGAN (Li et al., 2024 ) 
employed  an improved  symmetric  GAN architecture  to enhance  cross-
modality  adaptation,  yet it may suffer from increased  training  com-

plexity and sensitivity  to large domain  shifts, potentially  leading  to

2.2. Simultaneous  feature and image alignment  methods
Considering  that the advantages  of image alignment  and feature 
alignment  can be leveraged  to tackle domain  adaptation  problems,  
many recent studies adopt both strategies  concurrently.  For exam-
ple, Chen et al. (2020a ) introduced  SIFA, a novel framework  for cross-
modal medical  image segmentation  that effectively  fuses image and 
feature alignment.  Han et al. (2021 ) proposed  DSAN, a symmetric  adap-
tation network  designed  to achieve  bidirectional  alignment  between  
source and target domain  translation  sub-networks.  Moreover,  Ji and 
Chung (2023 ) developed  MA-UDA,  a transformer-based  approach  that 
incorporates  meta-attention  to enable a comprehensive  attention-based  
alignment  mechanism  at the feature level, in addition  to employing  
GANs for image-level  alignment.  Feng et al. (2023 ) proposed  an adap-
tive semantic  alignment  module  that reduces  inter-domain  discrepancy  
at the class level by aligning  prototype  representations  across do-
mains, where unreliable  pixels are filtered  out to obtain more robust 
and accurate  feature prototypes.  Additionally,  Jiang et al. (2024 ) pre-
sented a multi-feature  joint discriminative  domain  adaptation  method  
that simultaneously  leverages  both feature alignment  and edge align-
ment to enhance  unsupervised  domain  adaptation  for femur X-ray 
image segmentation.  Extending  this concept  to the detection  task, Li 
et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework

et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework  
that integrates  feature and image alignment  with adversarial  learning  
to improve  the robustness  of multi-center  bone tumor detection  on 
radiographs.
2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.
2.4. Prior knowledge  constraint  methods
Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-

source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-
tropy over target data while incorporating  anatomical  priors via KL 
divergence.  This method  effectively  handles  scenarios  where source 
images are unavailable  due to privacy  constraints.  Diao et al. (2024 ) 
developed  TSANet,  a two-stage  pipeline  combining  Fourier-based  style 
transfer  with anatomical  entropy  minimization.  While improving  seg-
mentation  accuracy,  its adaptability  is limited  in domains  with sig-
nificant  structural  variations.  Gupta et al. (2022 ) incorporated  topo-
logical constraints  to enforce  geometric  relationships  between  organs,  
though  its reliance  on annotated  data to identify  and refine critical 
pixels restricts  its application  in fully unsupervised  settings.  Kervadec  et al. (2019 ) designed  a volume-based  regularization  term for weakly-
supervised  segmentation,  while Zhou et al. (2019 ) used statistical  label 
distributions  with KL divergence  guidance.  Zheng et al. (2024 ) pro-
posed DDSP, which builds upon feature disentanglement  with semantic  
consistency  and domain  perturbation  to improve  pseudo-label  quality.  
However,  these methods  generally  require  dataset-specific  pre-analysis  
or explicit  anatomical  constraints,  limiting  their flexibility  in handling  
dynamic  domain  shifts.
In contrast,  our FAUDA-Net  introduces  a frequency-aware  con-
trastive  alignment  mechanism  that captures  both structural  consistency  
and stylistic  variance  through  adaptive  frequency-domain  learning.  Un-
like methods  that depend  on pre-defined  spatial constraints  or dataset-
specific  statistical  priors, our approach  leverages  phase and amplitude  
representations  to achieve  non-rigid  and dynamic  feature alignment  
across domains.  By integrating  frequency-domain  cues with contrastive  
learning,  FAUDA-Net  aligns features  without  requiring  annotated  data 
in the target domain  or pre-computed  constraints,  enabling  robust

5.1. Datasets
To comprehensively  evaluate  the performance  of our proposed  
method,  we conduct  experiments  on three publicly  available  medical  
image segmentation  datasets:  MMWHS17  (Gao et al., 2023 ) for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation,  BraTS21  (Han et al., 2021 ) 
for cross-sequence  brain glioma segmentation,  and PROMISE12  (Liu 
et al., 2020 ) for cross-site  prostate  segmentation.
(1) MMWHS17  Dataset:  The Multi-Modality  Whole Heart Segmen-
tation Challenge  2017 (MMWHS17)  dataset  is employed  for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation.  The dataset  contains  20 
MRI and 20 CT scans with corresponding  voxel-wise  annotations.  Fol-
lowing the experimental  setup in Zheng et al. (2024 ), we focus on four 
cardiac  structures:  ascending  aorta (AA), left atrium blood cavity (LAC), 
left ventricle  blood cavity (LVC), and left ventricle  myocardium  (MYO).  
We employ  a two-fold  cross-validation  strategy,  with 20 source domain  
scans and 10 target domain  scans for training,  and the remaining  10 
target scans for testing.  All scans are reoriented  to RAI orientation,  
cropped  to 128 × 128 × 128 voxels, and intensity-normalized  (CT: -
100 to 800 HU; MRI: 0.5th to 99.5th percentiles).  Bidirectional  domain  
adaptation  is performed  by alternating  MRI and CT as source domains.
(2) BraTS21  Dataset:  The BraTS21  Dataset  comprises  1251 MRI 
scans, each including  four modality  sequences  (T1, T1ce, T2, and 
FLAIR) and annotated  with tumor sub-regions.  To address  the distinct  
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences  
are chosen for bidirectional  domain  adaptation,  focusing  on the seg-
mentation  of the whole tumor region. The dataset  is partitioned  into 
500 scans per domain  for source and target training,  with an additional  
251 cases allocated  for validation  and testing.  All volumes  are pre-
processed  via brain-region  centering  and cropped  to a consistent  size of 
128 × 128 × 128. Intensity  values are normalized  based on the 0.5th 
to 99.5th percentile  range to reduce scanner-specific  variations.  This 
setup enables  a focused  evaluation  of domain  adaptation  under pro-
nounced  inter-modality  distribution  shifts, particularly  in the context  
of structural  and contrast  differences  between  T2 and FLAIR imaging.
(3) PROMISE12  Dataset:  The PROMISE12  challenge  dataset  is used 
for cross-site  prostate  segmentation,  comprising  T2-weighted  MRI scans 
collected  from two medical  centers  (BIDMC  and HK), with 12 cases 
from each site. We randomly  split the 12 target scans into two folds 
and perform  two-fold  cross-validation.  For preprocessing,  we manually  
crop the original  scans to focus on the prostate  region and resize all 
cropped  scans to 256 × 256 × 32 with RAI orientation.
5.2. Experimental  setup and evaluation  metrics
Implementation  details:  Experiments  were conducted  on an NVIDIA  
RTX 3090 GPU with 24 GB memory.  The model was implemented  in 
PyTorch  and optimized  using the Adam optimizer.  We adopted  a 3D 
U-Net as the encoder,  with the channel  configuration  for each layer set 
to [8, 16, 32, 64]. The pixel-wise  segmentation  decoder  comprises  two 
ResNet blocks and a convolutional  layer, where the output channels  
match the number  of classes.  To balance  training  stability  and adap-
tation efficiency,  we applied  differentiated  learning  rates: 1 × 10−4 for 
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder  
network.  The frequency  mixing ratio parameter  𝛽 was configured  as 
0.5 for the source domain  and 0.01 for the target domain,  while the 
enhancement  degree 𝑁 in spectral  regularization  was set to 30 for the 
source domain  and 10 for the target domain.
All models  were trained  using data derived  from the same pre-
processed  3D volumes.  We applied  an identical  pre-processing  pipeline  
(intensity  normalization  to [−1,1]) and the same set of data aug-
mentation  strategies  (random  rotation,  scaling,  affine transformations)  
across all experiments.  For the 2D methods,  slices were consistently  
extracted  from these 3D volumes  following  the practice  established  
in DDSP (using coronal  slices for MMWHS17,  axial slices for BraTS21  
and PROMISE12).  Crucially,  to ensure all methods  were evaluated  on the same ultimate  task of 3D segmentation,  the predictions  from all 
2D methods  were reconstructed  into complete  3D volumes.  Regarding  
the training  setup, for the 2D methods,  we followed  the training  
configuration  of SE-ASA,  using 50000 iterations.  For the 3D methods  
(FAUDA-Net  and DDSP),  we followed  the training  setting of DDSP, us-
ing 500 epochs.  Although  the core architectures  and parameter  counts 
naturally  differ between  2D and 3D networks,  we reproduced  the 
baselines  in the same computing  environment  as proposed  in their 
original  work.
Evaluation  metrics:  To evaluate  segmentation  quality,  we employed  
two complementary  evaluation  criteria:  the Dice Similarity  Coefficient  
(DSC) and Average  Surface  Distance  (ASD). DSC quantifies  the spatial 
agreement  between  predicted  segmentations  and their corresponding  
ground  truth annotations,  with values spanning  from 0 (indicating  com-
plete mismatch)  to 1 (representing  perfect alignment).  ASD provides  a 
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean 
distance  between  the surfaces  of predicted  and reference  structures,  
thereby  offering  sensitive  measurement  of contour  alignment  preci-
sion. DSC and ASD enable comprehensive  assessment  of both regional  
coverage  accuracy  and detailed  boundary  fidelity  in our segmentation  
results.
5.3. Comparison  with state-of-the-art  methods
The proposed  FAUDA-Net  is evaluated  against  eight state-of-the-art  
unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) methods:  (1) CycleGAN  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ) employs  cycle-consistent  generative  adversarial  networks  
to perform  unpaired  image-to-image  translation  between  domains,  (2)
SIFA (Chen et al., 2020a ) integrates  semantic-aware  image translation  
and feature alignment  in a unified  framework  to jointly adapt at pixel 
and feature levels, (3) DSAN (Han et al., 2021 ) introduces  a dual-
stream alignment  network  with domain-private  and shared components  
to reduce feature discrepancy  bidirectionally,  (4) SFDA (Bateson  et al., 
2022 ) formulates  a source-free  UDA strategy  that adapts models  via 
entropy  minimization  and class distribution  alignment  without  access-
ing source data, (5) SE-ASA  (Feng et al., 2023 ) employs  selective  
entropy  constraints  on confident  predictions  and adaptive  semantic  
alignment  to enhance  segmentation  consistency  across domains,  (6)
UNIT-DDPM  (Özbey et al., 2023 ) combines  denoising  diffusion  prob-
abilistic  models  with cycle-consistent  learning  to support  high-fidelity  
cross-domain  adaptation,  (7) SFS (Stan and Rostami , 2024 ) learns a 
domain-agnostic  feature representation  by projecting  both domains  
into a common  latent space with consistency  regularization,  and (8)
DDSP (Zheng et al., 2024 ) incorporates  semantic  preservation  into dis-
tribution  alignment  to prevent  structural  distortion  during adaptation.  
All comparative  results are reproduced  using official implementations

All comparative  results are reproduced  using official implementations  
with only necessary  adaptations  to accommodate  dataset  variations.  
To further evaluate  performance  in extreme  scenarios,  two reference

per_question_results.question: 腹腔镜图像语义分割的域适应方法为什么需要频率感知？
per_question_results.ground_truth: 腹腔镜图像语义分割需要频率感知是因为合成图像和真实腹腔镜图像之间存在显著的域差距（如光照、纹理、颜色等）。频率感知方法可以通过径向频率掩码选择性地掩蔽真实图像的频率分量，并通过 Mean Teacher 框架强制高频和低频表示之间的一致性，从而减少域差距，无需目标域的人工标注。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问，很高兴为您解答关于腹腔镜图像语义分割域适应中“频率感知”必要性的问题。

根据知识库中的两篇研究文献，腹腔镜图像的域适应需要频率感知，主要原因如下：

1. **模拟图像与真实图像存在显著的频率域差异**：真实腹腔镜图像包含丰富的高频细节（如复杂背景、纹理、血管、病变区域）和低频特性（如整体光照、颜色风格），而合成/模拟图像往往缺乏高频细节，且低频风格也不同。这种“频率域鸿沟”是导致模型在真实手术图像上性能下降的关键原因【来源：《applsci-16-00840-v2.pdf》】。

2. **高频与低频承载不同语义信息**：文献明确指出，“复杂 backgrounds and rich textures represent the high-frequency components”，而“lighting and style correspond to their low-frequency components”【来源：《applsci-16-00840-v2.pdf》】。因此，仅在空间域（如像素或特征图）做对齐，容易忽略结构（高频）与风格（低频）的解耦建模，导致边界模糊、结构失真等问题【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】。

3. **频率操作可提升鲁棒性与泛化性**：例如，Radial Frequency Masking（RFM）模块通过有选择地遮蔽高频/低频成分，迫使网络从残缺频谱中推理完整语义，从而学习更鲁棒、更具判别力的域不变表征【来源：《applsci-16-00840-v2.pdf》】；而FAUDA-Net进一步利用相位（编码结构）与幅度（编码风格）分别约束，实现“结构一致性”与“风格自适应”的协同优化【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】。

综上，频率感知并非辅助手段，而是针对腹腔镜图像特有域偏移（如光照不均、组织形变、器械反光、血渍干扰等）所提出的**机理驱动型解决方案**，能更本质地弥合模拟→真实之间的分布差距。

如您想深入了解某项技术（如RFM实现细节、BFDA公式推导或实验配置），欢迎随时告诉我，我可为您进一步梳理；若涉及具体代码、数据集使用或临床部署问题，也建议转接我们的技术专家为您提供一对一支持。祝您科研顺利！😊

Huiwen Dong

School of Information Science and Engineering, Lanzhou University, Lanzhou 730000, China;

Abstract
Semantic segmentation of laparoscopic images requires costly pixel-level annotations,
which are often unavailable for real surgical data. This gives rise to an unsupervised
domain adaptation scenario, where labeled synthetic images serve as the source domain and
unlabeled real images as the target. We propose a frequency-aware unsupervised domain
adaptation framework to mitigate the domain gap between simulated and real laparoscopic
images. Specifically, we introduce a Radial Frequency Masking module that selectively
masks frequency components of real images, and employ a Mean Teacher framework
to enforce consistency between high- and low-frequency representations. In addition,
we propose a module called Fourier Domain Adaptation-Blend, a style transfer strategy
based on low-frequency blending, and apply entropy minimization to enhance prediction
confidence on the target domain. Experiments are conducted on public datasets by jointly
training on simulated and real laparoscopic images. Our method consistently outperforms
representative baselines. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of frequency-aware
adaptation in surgical image segmentation without relying on manual annotations from
the target domain.

6. Conclusions
This paper studies unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for semantic segmen-
tation of laparoscopic images, aiming to bridge the domain shift between computer-
simulated data and real intra-operative scenes without requiring pixel-wise annotations in
the target domain.
We propose a frequency-aware UDA framework that combines (i) FDA-Blend for
appearance alignment in supervised source training, (ii) RFM to introduce structured
frequency perturbations for robust teacher–student consistency learning on unlabeled
target images, and (iii) Entropy Minimization to encourage confident and stable predictions
during self-training.
Scientific novelty. Differing from prior approaches that rely solely on spatial aug-
mentations or global style transfer, our method explicitly leverages frequency-domain
operations within a unified UDA pipeline. In particular, RFM provides a principled way to
regularize target-domain learning by selectively masking frequency components, which
promotes domain-invariant representations while preserving the semantic structure essen-
tial for surgical scene understanding. Together with FDA-Blend and entropy regularization,
the proposed design yields consistent improvements over representative UDA baselines
under both simulated →real and translated →real settings.
Practical significance. Our framework offers an effective solution to laparoscopic image
segmentation in real clinical data by primarily exploiting readily available simulated data,
substantially reducing the dependency on costly expert annotations for each new surgical
domain, device, or hospital. This makes the proposed method particularly appealing for
scalable deployment and rapid adaptation in data-scarce clinical environments.

1. Introduction
Deep neural networks  have significantly  advanced  medical  image 
segmentation  by leveraging  their powerful  feature extraction  capabil-
ities and effective  utilization  of annotated  datasets.  However,  these 
methods  typically  assume  that training  and testing data follow iden-
tical distribution  characteristics  and are often applied  within a single 
imaging  modality  (van Tulder and de Bruijne , 2018 ; Ouyang  et al., 
2022 ; Varoquaux  and Colliot , 2023 ). As shown in Fig.  1(a), real-
world medical  image analysis  scenarios  involve  significant  differences  
in contrast,  texture,  and intensity  between  modalities  such as MRI 
and CT, which challenges  this assumption.  These discrepancies  limit 
the generalization  capability  of conventional  models,  resulting  in sub-
optimal  performance  in cross-modal  applications.  In clinical  practice,  
utilizing  a model trained  on one modality  (e.g., MRI) to segment  images 
from another  modality  (e.g., CT) offers considerable  benefits:  it reduces  
annotation  costs and expands  the model’s  applicability.  Cross-modality  
(or cross-domain)  segmentation  capability  is clinically  significant,  as

2. Related  works
In this section,  we review recent advances  closely related to our 
work. These approaches  can be roughly  categorized  into four cate-
gories: (1) image alignment  methods,  (2) simultaneous  feature and 
image alignment  methods,  (3) disentangled  representation  learning  
methods,  and (4) prior knowledge  constraint  methods.
2.1. Image alignment  methods
Image alignment  methods  aim to reduce the domain  gap by trans-
forming  source-domain  images to mimic the style of the target domain.  
A common  strategy  involves  using image-to-image  translation  net-
works, such as cycle-consistent  adversarial  networks  (CycleGAN)  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ), to generate  semantically  consistent  target-style  images 
from the source domain.  Similarly,  Huo et al. (2018 ) employed  a 
translation  network  to synthesize  images with target-domain  charac-
teristics  and used these generated  images along with their labels to 
train a segmentation  model. Zhang et al. (2019 ) introduced  content  and 
style discriminators  to preserve  structural  semantics  and enforce  noise 
patterns  consistent  with the target domain,  respectively.  However,  
these methods  often suffer from semantic  distortions  and artifacts  in 
the translated  images,  limiting  their effectiveness.
Furthermore,  Henry et al. (2021 ) improved  semantic  preservation  
through  conditional  GANs and L1 loss, yet required  paired data, which 
restricts  its scalability.  Other style transfer  methods  such as AdaIN (Gu 
and Ye, 2021 ) adapted  feature statistics  to align styles but were highly 
sensitive  to hyperparameter  settings.  Recently,  ISGAN (Li et al., 2024 ) 
employed  an improved  symmetric  GAN architecture  to enhance  cross-
modality  adaptation,  yet it may suffer from increased  training  com-

2.2. Simultaneous  feature and image alignment  methods
Considering  that the advantages  of image alignment  and feature 
alignment  can be leveraged  to tackle domain  adaptation  problems,  
many recent studies adopt both strategies  concurrently.  For exam-
ple, Chen et al. (2020a ) introduced  SIFA, a novel framework  for cross-
modal medical  image segmentation  that effectively  fuses image and 
feature alignment.  Han et al. (2021 ) proposed  DSAN, a symmetric  adap-
tation network  designed  to achieve  bidirectional  alignment  between  
source and target domain  translation  sub-networks.  Moreover,  Ji and 
Chung (2023 ) developed  MA-UDA,  a transformer-based  approach  that 
incorporates  meta-attention  to enable a comprehensive  attention-based  
alignment  mechanism  at the feature level, in addition  to employing  
GANs for image-level  alignment.  Feng et al. (2023 ) proposed  an adap-
tive semantic  alignment  module  that reduces  inter-domain  discrepancy  
at the class level by aligning  prototype  representations  across do-
mains, where unreliable  pixels are filtered  out to obtain more robust 
and accurate  feature prototypes.  Additionally,  Jiang et al. (2024 ) pre-
sented a multi-feature  joint discriminative  domain  adaptation  method  
that simultaneously  leverages  both feature alignment  and edge align-
ment to enhance  unsupervised  domain  adaptation  for femur X-ray 
image segmentation.  Extending  this concept  to the detection  task, Li 
et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework

2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.

Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-
