5.1. Datasets
To comprehensively  evaluate  the performance  of our proposed  
method,  we conduct  experiments  on three publicly  available  medical  
image segmentation  datasets:  MMWHS17  (Gao et al., 2023 ) for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation,  BraTS21  (Han et al., 2021 ) 
for cross-sequence  brain glioma segmentation,  and PROMISE12  (Liu 
et al., 2020 ) for cross-site  prostate  segmentation.
(1) MMWHS17  Dataset:  The Multi-Modality  Whole Heart Segmen-
tation Challenge  2017 (MMWHS17)  dataset  is employed  for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation.  The dataset  contains  20 
MRI and 20 CT scans with corresponding  voxel-wise  annotations.  Fol-
lowing the experimental  setup in Zheng et al. (2024 ), we focus on four 
cardiac  structures:  ascending  aorta (AA), left atrium blood cavity (LAC), 
left ventricle  blood cavity (LVC), and left ventricle  myocardium  (MYO).  
We employ  a two-fold  cross-validation  strategy,  with 20 source domain  
scans and 10 target domain  scans for training,  and the remaining  10 
target scans for testing.  All scans are reoriented  to RAI orientation,  
cropped  to 128 × 128 × 128 voxels, and intensity-normalized  (CT: -
100 to 800 HU; MRI: 0.5th to 99.5th percentiles).  Bidirectional  domain  
adaptation  is performed  by alternating  MRI and CT as source domains.
(2) BraTS21  Dataset:  The BraTS21  Dataset  comprises  1251 MRI 
scans, each including  four modality  sequences  (T1, T1ce, T2, and 
FLAIR) and annotated  with tumor sub-regions.  To address  the distinct  
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences  
are chosen for bidirectional  domain  adaptation,  focusing  on the seg-
mentation  of the whole tumor region. The dataset  is partitioned  into 
500 scans per domain  for source and target training,  with an additional  
251 cases allocated  for validation  and testing.  All volumes  are pre-
processed  via brain-region  centering  and cropped  to a consistent  size of 
128 × 128 × 128. Intensity  values are normalized  based on the 0.5th 
to 99.5th percentile  range to reduce scanner-specific  variations.  This 
setup enables  a focused  evaluation  of domain  adaptation  under pro-
nounced  inter-modality  distribution  shifts, particularly  in the context  
of structural  and contrast  differences  between  T2 and FLAIR imaging.
(3) PROMISE12  Dataset:  The PROMISE12  challenge  dataset  is used 
for cross-site  prostate  segmentation,  comprising  T2-weighted  MRI scans 
collected  from two medical  centers  (BIDMC  and HK), with 12 cases 
from each site. We randomly  split the 12 target scans into two folds 
and perform  two-fold  cross-validation.  For preprocessing,  we manually  
crop the original  scans to focus on the prostate  region and resize all 
cropped  scans to 256 × 256 × 32 with RAI orientation.
5.2. Experimental  setup and evaluation  metrics
Implementation  details:  Experiments  were conducted  on an NVIDIA  
RTX 3090 GPU with 24 GB memory.  The model was implemented  in 
PyTorch  and optimized  using the Adam optimizer.  We adopted  a 3D 
U-Net as the encoder,  with the channel  configuration  for each layer set 
to [8, 16, 32, 64]. The pixel-wise  segmentation  decoder  comprises  two 
ResNet blocks and a convolutional  layer, where the output channels  
match the number  of classes.  To balance  training  stability  and adap-
tation efficiency,  we applied  differentiated  learning  rates: 1 × 10−4 for 
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder  
network.  The frequency  mixing ratio parameter  𝛽 was configured  as 
0.5 for the source domain  and 0.01 for the target domain,  while the 
enhancement  degree 𝑁 in spectral  regularization  was set to 30 for the 
source domain  and 10 for the target domain.
All models  were trained  using data derived  from the same pre-
processed  3D volumes.  We applied  an identical  pre-processing  pipeline  
(intensity  normalization  to [−1,1]) and the same set of data aug-
mentation  strategies  (random  rotation,  scaling,  affine transformations)  
across all experiments.  For the 2D methods,  slices were consistently  
extracted  from these 3D volumes  following  the practice  established  
in DDSP (using coronal  slices for MMWHS17,  axial slices for BraTS21  
and PROMISE12).  Crucially,  to ensure all methods  were evaluated  on the same ultimate  task of 3D segmentation,  the predictions  from all 
2D methods  were reconstructed  into complete  3D volumes.  Regarding  
the training  setup, for the 2D methods,  we followed  the training  
configuration  of SE-ASA,  using 50000 iterations.  For the 3D methods  
(FAUDA-Net  and DDSP),  we followed  the training  setting of DDSP, us-
ing 500 epochs.  Although  the core architectures  and parameter  counts 
naturally  differ between  2D and 3D networks,  we reproduced  the 
baselines  in the same computing  environment  as proposed  in their 
original  work.
Evaluation  metrics:  To evaluate  segmentation  quality,  we employed  
two complementary  evaluation  criteria:  the Dice Similarity  Coefficient  
(DSC) and Average  Surface  Distance  (ASD). DSC quantifies  the spatial 
agreement  between  predicted  segmentations  and their corresponding  
ground  truth annotations,  with values spanning  from 0 (indicating  com-
plete mismatch)  to 1 (representing  perfect alignment).  ASD provides  a 
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean

complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean 
distance  between  the surfaces  of predicted  and reference  structures,  
thereby  offering  sensitive  measurement  of contour  alignment  preci-
sion. DSC and ASD enable comprehensive  assessment  of both regional  
coverage  accuracy  and detailed  boundary  fidelity  in our segmentation  
results.
5.3. Comparison  with state-of-the-art  methods
The proposed  FAUDA-Net  is evaluated  against  eight state-of-the-art  
unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) methods:  (1) CycleGAN  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ) employs  cycle-consistent  generative  adversarial  networks  
to perform  unpaired  image-to-image  translation  between  domains,  (2)
SIFA (Chen et al., 2020a ) integrates  semantic-aware  image translation  
and feature alignment  in a unified  framework  to jointly adapt at pixel 
and feature levels, (3) DSAN (Han et al., 2021 ) introduces  a dual-
stream alignment  network  with domain-private  and shared components  
to reduce feature discrepancy  bidirectionally,  (4) SFDA (Bateson  et al., 
2022 ) formulates  a source-free  UDA strategy  that adapts models  via 
entropy  minimization  and class distribution  alignment  without  access-
ing source data, (5) SE-ASA  (Feng et al., 2023 ) employs  selective  
entropy  constraints  on confident  predictions  and adaptive  semantic  
alignment  to enhance  segmentation  consistency  across domains,  (6)
UNIT-DDPM  (Özbey et al., 2023 ) combines  denoising  diffusion  prob-
abilistic  models  with cycle-consistent  learning  to support  high-fidelity  
cross-domain  adaptation,  (7) SFS (Stan and Rostami , 2024 ) learns a 
domain-agnostic  feature representation  by projecting  both domains  
into a common  latent space with consistency  regularization,  and (8)
DDSP (Zheng et al., 2024 ) incorporates  semantic  preservation  into dis-
tribution  alignment  to prevent  structural  distortion  during adaptation.

per_question_results.ground_truth: MPSCL（Margin Preserving Self-paced Contrastive Learning）利用域自适应类别原型来构建正负样本对，并通过渐进式细化的语义原型指导，提出了一种保持边界的对比损失，以增强嵌入表示空间的判别性。同时，通过自步方式生成更多有信息的伪标签，增强对比学习的监督。

您好！感谢您的提问。作为客服代表，我很乐意为您专业解答关于MPSCL方法如何解决医学图像分割中对比学习的类别对齐问题。

根据知识库内容，MPSCL（Margin Preserving Self-paced Contrastive Learning）通过以下核心机制解决类别对齐问题：

1. **引入域自适应类别原型（Domain-adaptive Category Prototypes）作为类别锚点**：  
   不同于传统对比学习中依赖数据增强构造正负样本对，MPSCL利用源域先验知识构建类别原型，并将其作为正/负样本对的锚点，从而在特征空间中显式引导跨域类别级对齐【来源：《2103.08454v1.pdf》】。

2. **构建类别感知的对比学习目标**：

3. **结合自步伪标签（Self-paced Pseudo-labels）实现目标域监督**：

V. C ONCLUSIONS
For the challenge of unsupervised domain adaptation in
medical image segmentation, an innovative MPSCL model is
proposed, which promotes category-aware feature alignment
by cross-domain contrastive learning. To the best of our knowl-
edge, this is the ﬁrst time to introduce contrastive learning for
this practical problem. Specially, the domain-adaptive category
prototypes are exploited to constitute contrastive pairs for
the joint contrastive learning between the two domains. Wegenerate informative self-paced pseudo-labels for target do-
main to perform contrastive learning in target domain without
prior label available. The discriminability of representation is
boosted by a margin preserving contrastive learning loss. It is
worth noticing that one category prototype per category does
not cover the overall distribution. Thus, our ongoing research
work includes learning prototypes adaptively with the data
distribution.

Zhizhe Liu, Zhenfeng Zhu, Shuai Zheng, Y ang Liu, Jiayu Zhou, and Y ao Zhao, Senior Member, IEEE,
Abstract — To bridge the gap between the source and
target domains in unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA),
the most common strategy puts focus on matching the
marginal distributions in the feature space through ad-
versarial learning. However, such category-agnostic global
alignment lacks of exploiting the class-level joint distribu-
tions, causing the aligned distribution less discriminative.
To address this issue, we propose in this paper a novel
margin preserving self-paced contrastive Learning (MP-
SCL) model for cross-modal medical image segmentation.
Unlike the conventional construction of contrastive pairs
in contrastive learning, the domain-adaptive category pro-
totypes are utilized to constitute the positive and negative
sample pairs. With the guidance of progressively reﬁned
semantic prototypes, a novel margin preserving contrastive
loss is proposed to boost the discriminability of embed-
ded representation space. To enhance the supervision
for contrastive learning, more informative pseudo-labels
are generated in target domain in a self-paced way, thus
beneﬁting the category-aware distribution alignment for
UDA. Furthermore, the domain-invariant representations
are learned through joint contrastive learning between the
two domains. Extensive experiments on cross-modal car-
diac segmentation tasks demonstrate that MPSCL signiﬁ-
cantly improves semantic segmentation performance, and
outperforms a wide variety of state-of-the-art methods by a
large margin.
Index Terms — unsupervised domain adaptation, image
segmentation, contrastive learning, adversarial learning.

5. Discussion
In clinical practice, multiple imaging modalities are often com-
bined to aid in diagnosis since different modalities of the sameanatomy are complementary [73]. The deep convolutional neural
network can accurately segment multi-modality images when
annotations are provided for each modality image. However, it is
prohibitively expensive or sometimes even infeasible to annotate
data for all modalities, and the model trained by a single modality
is difﬁcult to generalize to other modalities due to the domain
shift. To alleviate the burden of data annotation, some works
focused on alleviating the domain shift and proposed unsupervised
domain adaptation methods, making the model trained on label-
rich source data better generalize the unlabeled target domain.
Along this promising direction, we put forward a novel unsuper-
vised domain adaptation method, without extra annotation effort,our method greatly improves the generalization of cross-modality
data.

in the semantic level and construct enough contrastive pairs.

in SSL, the domain-adaptive prototypes are utilized in our

of contrastive pairs in feature space for contrastive learning.

Self-training, which typically includes a teacher-student
framework, uses a good teacher model trained on the labeleddata to assign pseudo-labels to the unlabeled data, and then uti-
lizes human labels and pseudo-labels to jointly train a student
model. In deep learning, self-training has received increasing
interest due to the dramatic reduction in cost of data labeling
(e.g., image classiﬁcation [32], machine translation [33] and
speech recognition [34]). Recently, some UDA works [18],
[20], [35] have attempted to generate pseudo-labels for the
target data to achieve category-aware domain alignment. For
example, [20] leveraged an anchor-based pixel-level distance
loss to match the joint distributions between the two domains
in the feature space by self-training. But, since it fails to make
full use of local semantic structure information, the knowledge

per_question_results.ground_truth: 局部对比损失通过利用伪标签获得的语义标签信息，学习对分割有用的像素级特征。与基于随机增强和空间邻近性定义相似区域的方法不同，该方法基于语义标签定义局部区域的相似性和差异性，从而提升分割精度。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问。关于局部对比损失在半监督医学图像分割中的作用，根据知识库内容，其核心作用可归纳为以下三点：

1. 学习更有效的像素级特征表示：局部对比损失旨在鼓励属于同一语义类别（即相同真实标签或伪标签）的像素在特征空间中具有相似的表示，同时使不同类别的像素表示相互远离。这种设计特别针对分割任务对局部细节敏感的特点，弥补了仅依赖全局对比损失的不足【来源：《2112.09645v1.pdf》】。

2. 充分利用有限标注与大量无标注数据：该方法结合伪标签进行自训练，在仅有少量标注图像的情况下，利用模型对无标注图像生成的伪标签来构建局部对比关系。对比损失同时作用于标注集和无标注集，而分割损失仅作用于标注集，从而提升模型在标注稀缺场景下的泛化能力【来源：《2112.09645v1.pdf》】。

3. 解决传统无监督/半监督局部对比方法的局限性：相比依赖随机增强或空间邻近性定义正负样本的方法，本文提出的局部对比损失以语义一致的伪标签为依据，避免了因缺乏真实标注而导致的语义错配问题；也优于基于超像素（如SLIC）等无监督分割生成的代理标签，因其无法跨图像保持解剖结构的一致标签ID【来源：《2112.09645v1.pdf》】。

需要说明的是，知识库中未涉及该损失的具体数学形式、超参数设置或与其他损失（如Dice损失）的权重平衡细节。如您需了解实现细节、代码结构或实验配置等更深入的技术信息，建议转接人工客服，我们将为您安排技术专家进一步协助。

Abstract —Supervised deep learning-based methods yield
accurate results for medical image segmentation. However, they
require large labeled datasets for this, and obtaining them
is a laborious task that requires clinical expertise. Semi/self-
supervised learning-based approaches address this limitation
by exploiting unlabeled data along with limited annotated data.
Recent self-supervised learning methods use contrastive loss to
learn good global level representations from unlabeled images
and achieve high performance in classiﬁcation tasks on popular
natural image datasets like ImageNet. In pixel-level prediction
tasks such as segmentation, it is crucial to also learn good
local level representations along with global representations to
achieve better accuracy. However, the impact of the existing
local contrastive loss-based methods remains limited for learning
good local representations because similar and dissimilar local
regions are deﬁned based on random augmentations and
spatial proximity; not based on the semantic label of local
regions due to lack of large-scale expert annotations in the
semi/self-supervised setting. In this paper, we propose a local
contrastive loss to learn good pixel level features useful for
segmentation by exploiting semantic label information obtained
from pseudo-labels of unlabeled images alongside limited
annotated images. In particular, we deﬁne the proposed loss
to encourage similar representations for the pixels that have
the same pseudo-label/ label while being dissimilar to the
representation of pixels with different pseudo-label/label in the
dataset. We perform pseudo-label based self-training and train
the network by jointly optimizing the proposed contrastive
loss on both labeled and unlabeled sets and segmentation loss
on only the limited labeled set. We evaluated the proposed

Unsupervised  domain adaptation  (UDA) has achieved  notable advances  in medical  image segmentation.  
However,  the significant  domain shifts between  source and target data continue  to pose fundamental  
challenges,  driving an urgent demand  for more robust cross-domain  solutions.  Current UDA methods  often 
rely on static spatial alignment  strategies  that ignore the dynamic  evolution  of feature distributions  during 
training,  often resulting  in blurred boundary  delineation  and loss of structural  details. To address these issues, 
we propose  a frequency-aware  unsupervised  domain adaptation  network  (FAUDA-Net),  which dynamically  
adapts to feature distribution  shifts and enhances  boundary  delineation  in the target domain.  Specifically,  
FAUDA-Net  introduces  dual-domain  distribution  disruption  to encourage  domain-invariant  representations,  
along with frequency  constraints,  that leverage  both phase and amplitude  components  to guide cross-domain  
adaptation.  Furthermore,  a frequency-aware  contrastive  learning  mechanism  aligns source and target features  
through  channel  self-attention  matrices,  enabling  a shared pixel-wise  decoder  to achieve robust segmentation

through  channel  self-attention  matrices,  enabling  a shared pixel-wise  decoder  to achieve robust segmentation  
performance.  Extensive  experiments  on three representative  medical  image datasets,  MMWHS17,  BraTS21,  
and PROMISE12,  demonstrate  that FAUDA-Net  outperforms  eight state-of-the-art  methods  in both overall 
segmentation  accuracy  (Dice) and boundary  extraction  precision  (ASD), providing  a reliable and effective

1. Introduction
Deep neural networks  have significantly  advanced  medical  image 
segmentation  by leveraging  their powerful  feature extraction  capabil-
ities and effective  utilization  of annotated  datasets.  However,  these 
methods  typically  assume  that training  and testing data follow iden-
tical distribution  characteristics  and are often applied  within a single 
imaging  modality  (van Tulder and de Bruijne , 2018 ; Ouyang  et al., 
2022 ; Varoquaux  and Colliot , 2023 ). As shown in Fig.  1(a), real-
world medical  image analysis  scenarios  involve  significant  differences  
in contrast,  texture,  and intensity  between  modalities  such as MRI 
and CT, which challenges  this assumption.  These discrepancies  limit 
the generalization  capability  of conventional  models,  resulting  in sub-
optimal  performance  in cross-modal  applications.  In clinical  practice,  
utilizing  a model trained  on one modality  (e.g., MRI) to segment  images 
from another  modality  (e.g., CT) offers considerable  benefits:  it reduces  
annotation  costs and expands  the model’s  applicability.  Cross-modality  
(or cross-domain)  segmentation  capability  is clinically  significant,  as

As illustrated  in Fig.  1(b), unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) 
provides  an effective  solution  to mitigate  distribution  discrepancies  be-
tween source (training)  and target (testing)  data (Ganin and Lempitsky , 
2015 ; Hou et al., 2016 ; Cui et al., 2021 ; Liu et al., 2022 ). By em-
ploying  feature alignment  techniques,  UDA enables  models  to achieve  
segmentation  performance  on the target domain  comparable  to that 
on the source domain  without  requiring  annotations  for target data, 
significantly  reducing  labeling  costs and enhancing  the practicality  of 
deep learning  methods  in clinical  applications.  Developing  effective  
UDA methods  is thus critically  important  for cross-domain  medical  
image segmentation.  The primary  goal of UDA is to address  distribution  
shifts between  source and target domains,  which represents  a com-
mon challenge  in real-world  applications.  Early UDA methods  utilized  
generative  adversarial  networks  (GANs)  for pixel-level  style transfer,  
translating  source images into the style of the target domain  (Zhu et al.,

The introduction  of adversarial  learning  based on feature align-
ment has significantly  advanced  domain  adaptation  through  the use 
of domain  classifiers  and adversarial  training  mechanisms  to align 
cross-domain  features,  thereby  enhancing  model generalization  (Zhang

these methods  remain challenged  by training  instability  and mode

spatial domain,  ignoring  the dynamic  evolution  of feature distribu-

model structural  details and boundary  regions  in the target domain.

role of frequency-domain  information  in capturing  structural  semantics  
and cross-domain  distribution  differences,  which restricts  their ability 
to learn domain-invariant  features  effectively.  In fact, the phase and 
amplitude  components  of the frequency  domain  encode structural  in-
formation  and stylistic  variations,  respectively,  offering  rich cues for 
discriminative  and dynamic  domain  alignment.  Therefore,  developing  
an adaptive  framework  that can perceive  distribution  dynamics,  incor-

2. Related  works
In this section,  we review recent advances  closely related to our 
work. These approaches  can be roughly  categorized  into four cate-
gories: (1) image alignment  methods,  (2) simultaneous  feature and 
image alignment  methods,  (3) disentangled  representation  learning  
methods,  and (4) prior knowledge  constraint  methods.
2.1. Image alignment  methods
Image alignment  methods  aim to reduce the domain  gap by trans-
forming  source-domain  images to mimic the style of the target domain.  
A common  strategy  involves  using image-to-image  translation  net-
works, such as cycle-consistent  adversarial  networks  (CycleGAN)  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ), to generate  semantically  consistent  target-style  images 
from the source domain.  Similarly,  Huo et al. (2018 ) employed  a 
translation  network  to synthesize  images with target-domain  charac-
teristics  and used these generated  images along with their labels to 
train a segmentation  model. Zhang et al. (2019 ) introduced  content  and 
style discriminators  to preserve  structural  semantics  and enforce  noise 
patterns  consistent  with the target domain,  respectively.  However,  
these methods  often suffer from semantic  distortions  and artifacts  in 
the translated  images,  limiting  their effectiveness.
Furthermore,  Henry et al. (2021 ) improved  semantic  preservation  
through  conditional  GANs and L1 loss, yet required  paired data, which 
restricts  its scalability.  Other style transfer  methods  such as AdaIN (Gu 
and Ye, 2021 ) adapted  feature statistics  to align styles but were highly 
sensitive  to hyperparameter  settings.  Recently,  ISGAN (Li et al., 2024 ) 
employed  an improved  symmetric  GAN architecture  to enhance  cross-
modality  adaptation,  yet it may suffer from increased  training  com-

2.2. Simultaneous  feature and image alignment  methods
Considering  that the advantages  of image alignment  and feature 
alignment  can be leveraged  to tackle domain  adaptation  problems,  
many recent studies adopt both strategies  concurrently.  For exam-
ple, Chen et al. (2020a ) introduced  SIFA, a novel framework  for cross-
modal medical  image segmentation  that effectively  fuses image and 
feature alignment.  Han et al. (2021 ) proposed  DSAN, a symmetric  adap-
tation network  designed  to achieve  bidirectional  alignment  between  
source and target domain  translation  sub-networks.  Moreover,  Ji and 
Chung (2023 ) developed  MA-UDA,  a transformer-based  approach  that 
incorporates  meta-attention  to enable a comprehensive  attention-based  
alignment  mechanism  at the feature level, in addition  to employing  
GANs for image-level  alignment.  Feng et al. (2023 ) proposed  an adap-
tive semantic  alignment  module  that reduces  inter-domain  discrepancy  
at the class level by aligning  prototype  representations  across do-
mains, where unreliable  pixels are filtered  out to obtain more robust 
and accurate  feature prototypes.  Additionally,  Jiang et al. (2024 ) pre-
sented a multi-feature  joint discriminative  domain  adaptation  method  
that simultaneously  leverages  both feature alignment  and edge align-
ment to enhance  unsupervised  domain  adaptation  for femur X-ray 
image segmentation.  Extending  this concept  to the detection  task, Li 
et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework

et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework  
that integrates  feature and image alignment  with adversarial  learning  
to improve  the robustness  of multi-center  bone tumor detection  on 
radiographs.
2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.
2.4. Prior knowledge  constraint  methods
Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-

tropy over target data while incorporating  anatomical  priors via KL 
divergence.  This method  effectively  handles  scenarios  where source 
images are unavailable  due to privacy  constraints.  Diao et al. (2024 ) 
developed  TSANet,  a two-stage  pipeline  combining  Fourier-based  style 
transfer  with anatomical  entropy  minimization.  While improving  seg-

logical constraints  to enforce  geometric  relationships  between  organs,  
though  its reliance  on annotated  data to identify  and refine critical 
pixels restricts  its application  in fully unsupervised  settings.  Kervadec  et al. (2019 ) designed  a volume-based  regularization  term for weakly-
supervised  segmentation,  while Zhou et al. (2019 ) used statistical  label 
distributions  with KL divergence  guidance.  Zheng et al. (2024 ) pro-
posed DDSP, which builds upon feature disentanglement  with semantic  
consistency  and domain  perturbation  to improve  pseudo-label  quality.  
However,  these methods  generally  require  dataset-specific  pre-analysis  
or explicit  anatomical  constraints,  limiting  their flexibility  in handling  
dynamic  domain  shifts.
In contrast,  our FAUDA-Net  introduces  a frequency-aware  con-
trastive  alignment  mechanism  that captures  both structural  consistency  
and stylistic  variance  through  adaptive  frequency-domain  learning.  Un-
like methods  that depend  on pre-defined  spatial constraints  or dataset-
specific  statistical  priors, our approach  leverages  phase and amplitude  
representations  to achieve  non-rigid  and dynamic  feature alignment  
across domains.  By integrating  frequency-domain  cues with contrastive  
learning,  FAUDA-Net  aligns features  without  requiring  annotated  data 
in the target domain  or pre-computed  constraints,  enabling  robust

5.1. Datasets
To comprehensively  evaluate  the performance  of our proposed  
method,  we conduct  experiments  on three publicly  available  medical  
image segmentation  datasets:  MMWHS17  (Gao et al., 2023 ) for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation,  BraTS21  (Han et al., 2021 ) 
for cross-sequence  brain glioma segmentation,  and PROMISE12  (Liu 
et al., 2020 ) for cross-site  prostate  segmentation.
(1) MMWHS17  Dataset:  The Multi-Modality  Whole Heart Segmen-
tation Challenge  2017 (MMWHS17)  dataset  is employed  for cross-
modality  cardiac  substructure  segmentation.  The dataset  contains  20 
MRI and 20 CT scans with corresponding  voxel-wise  annotations.  Fol-
lowing the experimental  setup in Zheng et al. (2024 ), we focus on four 
cardiac  structures:  ascending  aorta (AA), left atrium blood cavity (LAC), 
left ventricle  blood cavity (LVC), and left ventricle  myocardium  (MYO).  
We employ  a two-fold  cross-validation  strategy,  with 20 source domain  
scans and 10 target domain  scans for training,  and the remaining  10 
target scans for testing.  All scans are reoriented  to RAI orientation,  
cropped  to 128 × 128 × 128 voxels, and intensity-normalized  (CT: -
100 to 800 HU; MRI: 0.5th to 99.5th percentiles).  Bidirectional  domain  
adaptation  is performed  by alternating  MRI and CT as source domains.
(2) BraTS21  Dataset:  The BraTS21  Dataset  comprises  1251 MRI 
scans, each including  four modality  sequences  (T1, T1ce, T2, and 
FLAIR) and annotated  with tumor sub-regions.  To address  the distinct  
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
tissue contrasts  offered  by different  sequences,  T2 and FLAIR sequences  
are chosen for bidirectional  domain  adaptation,  focusing  on the seg-
mentation  of the whole tumor region. The dataset  is partitioned  into 
500 scans per domain  for source and target training,  with an additional  
251 cases allocated  for validation  and testing.  All volumes  are pre-
processed  via brain-region  centering  and cropped  to a consistent  size of 
128 × 128 × 128. Intensity  values are normalized  based on the 0.5th 
to 99.5th percentile  range to reduce scanner-specific  variations.  This 
setup enables  a focused  evaluation  of domain  adaptation  under pro-
nounced  inter-modality  distribution  shifts, particularly  in the context  
of structural  and contrast  differences  between  T2 and FLAIR imaging.
(3) PROMISE12  Dataset:  The PROMISE12  challenge  dataset  is used 
for cross-site  prostate  segmentation,  comprising  T2-weighted  MRI scans 
collected  from two medical  centers  (BIDMC  and HK), with 12 cases 
from each site. We randomly  split the 12 target scans into two folds 
and perform  two-fold  cross-validation.  For preprocessing,  we manually  
crop the original  scans to focus on the prostate  region and resize all 
cropped  scans to 256 × 256 × 32 with RAI orientation.
5.2. Experimental  setup and evaluation  metrics
Implementation  details:  Experiments  were conducted  on an NVIDIA  
RTX 3090 GPU with 24 GB memory.  The model was implemented  in 
PyTorch  and optimized  using the Adam optimizer.  We adopted  a 3D 
U-Net as the encoder,  with the channel  configuration  for each layer set 
to [8, 16, 32, 64]. The pixel-wise  segmentation  decoder  comprises  two 
ResNet blocks and a convolutional  layer, where the output channels  
match the number  of classes.  To balance  training  stability  and adap-
tation efficiency,  we applied  differentiated  learning  rates: 1 × 10−4 for 
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
the shared encoder  and 1 × 10−3 for the shared segmentation  decoder  
network.  The frequency  mixing ratio parameter  𝛽 was configured  as 
0.5 for the source domain  and 0.01 for the target domain,  while the 
enhancement  degree 𝑁 in spectral  regularization  was set to 30 for the 
source domain  and 10 for the target domain.
All models  were trained  using data derived  from the same pre-
processed  3D volumes.  We applied  an identical  pre-processing  pipeline  
(intensity  normalization  to [−1,1]) and the same set of data aug-
mentation  strategies  (random  rotation,  scaling,  affine transformations)  
across all experiments.  For the 2D methods,  slices were consistently  
extracted  from these 3D volumes  following  the practice  established  
in DDSP (using coronal  slices for MMWHS17,  axial slices for BraTS21  
and PROMISE12).  Crucially,  to ensure all methods  were evaluated  on the same ultimate  task of 3D segmentation,  the predictions  from all 
2D methods  were reconstructed  into complete  3D volumes.  Regarding  
the training  setup, for the 2D methods,  we followed  the training  
configuration  of SE-ASA,  using 50000 iterations.  For the 3D methods  
(FAUDA-Net  and DDSP),  we followed  the training  setting of DDSP, us-
ing 500 epochs.  Although  the core architectures  and parameter  counts 
naturally  differ between  2D and 3D networks,  we reproduced  the 
baselines  in the same computing  environment  as proposed  in their 
original  work.
Evaluation  metrics:  To evaluate  segmentation  quality,  we employed  
two complementary  evaluation  criteria:  the Dice Similarity  Coefficient  
(DSC) and Average  Surface  Distance  (ASD). DSC quantifies  the spatial 
agreement  between  predicted  segmentations  and their corresponding  
ground  truth annotations,  with values spanning  from 0 (indicating  com-
plete mismatch)  to 1 (representing  perfect alignment).  ASD provides  a 
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean 
distance  between  the surfaces  of predicted  and reference  structures,  
thereby  offering  sensitive  measurement  of contour  alignment  preci-
sion. DSC and ASD enable comprehensive  assessment  of both regional  
coverage  accuracy  and detailed  boundary  fidelity  in our segmentation  
results.
5.3. Comparison  with state-of-the-art  methods
The proposed  FAUDA-Net  is evaluated  against  eight state-of-the-art  
unsupervised  domain  adaptation  (UDA) methods:  (1) CycleGAN  (Zhu 
et al., 2017 ) employs  cycle-consistent  generative  adversarial  networks  
to perform  unpaired  image-to-image  translation  between  domains,  (2)
SIFA (Chen et al., 2020a ) integrates  semantic-aware  image translation  
and feature alignment  in a unified  framework  to jointly adapt at pixel 
and feature levels, (3) DSAN (Han et al., 2021 ) introduces  a dual-
stream alignment  network  with domain-private  and shared components  
to reduce feature discrepancy  bidirectionally,  (4) SFDA (Bateson  et al., 
2022 ) formulates  a source-free  UDA strategy  that adapts models  via 
entropy  minimization  and class distribution  alignment  without  access-
ing source data, (5) SE-ASA  (Feng et al., 2023 ) employs  selective  
entropy  constraints  on confident  predictions  and adaptive  semantic  
alignment  to enhance  segmentation  consistency  across domains,  (6)
UNIT-DDPM  (Özbey et al., 2023 ) combines  denoising  diffusion  prob-
abilistic  models  with cycle-consistent  learning  to support  high-fidelity  
cross-domain  adaptation,  (7) SFS (Stan and Rostami , 2024 ) learns a 
domain-agnostic  feature representation  by projecting  both domains  
into a common  latent space with consistency  regularization,  and (8)
DDSP (Zheng et al., 2024 ) incorporates  semantic  preservation  into dis-
tribution  alignment  to prevent  structural  distortion  during adaptation.  
All comparative  results are reproduced  using official implementations

All comparative  results are reproduced  using official implementations  
with only necessary  adaptations  to accommodate  dataset  variations.

benchmarks  are included:  a lower bound (‘‘w/o DA’’), where the model

per_question_results.question: SimCLR 框架中哪些因素对对比学习的效果影响最大？
per_question_results.ground_truth: SimCLR 发现三个关键因素：(1) 数据增强的组合在定义有效的预测任务中起关键作用；(2) 在表示和对比损失之间引入可学习的非线性变换能显著提高学习表示的质量；(3) 对比学习受益于更大的 batch size 和更多的训练步骤。
per_question_results.source_doc: ASimple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问～作为客服代表，我很乐意为您解答关于SimCLR框架的问题。

根据知识库中《A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf》的系统性研究，以下四个因素被明确指出对对比学习效果影响最大，且均有实验证据支持：

1. **数据增强的组合方式**：单一增强操作（如仅随机裁剪）不足以学习高质量表征；而组合多种增强（如随机裁剪 + 颜色失真 + 高斯模糊）能显著提升性能。文中特别强调：“Composition of multiple data augmentation operations is crucial in defining the contrastive prediction tasks that yield effective representations”【来源：《ASimple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf》】。

2. **非线性投影头（learnable nonlinear transformation）**：在表征向量h和对比损失之间引入可学习的非线性映射g(h)（如MLP），能大幅提升表征质量。“Introducing a learnable nonlinear transformation between the representation and the contrastive loss substantially improves the quality of the learned representations”【来源：《ASimple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf》】。

3. **归一化嵌入与温度参数调优**：使用ℓ²归一化嵌入（即余弦相似度）并配合合适的温度参数τ，对NT-Xent损失至关重要；“without ℓ² normalization and proper temperature scaling, performance is significantly worse”【来源：《ASimple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf》】。

4. **更大的批量大小与更长的训练时间**：对比学习比监督学习更受益于大batch（如4096）和长epoch（如1000）；“Contrastive learning benefits from larger batch sizes and longer training compared to its supervised counterpart”，且“larger batch sizes provide more negative examples, facilitating convergence”【来源：《ASimple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf》】。

此外，网络深度与宽度（如ResNet-50 ×4）也被证实有正向影响【来源：《ASimple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations.pdf》】。

以上结论均来自SimCLR论文的系统消融实验与分析，具有充分依据。如您想了解某一项的具体实现细节（例如温度参数如何设置、投影头结构等），欢迎随时告诉我，我可以为您进一步定位原文内容 😊

如需技术实现指导或代码级问题，建议转接人工技术支持工程师，他们可为您提供更深入的协助。

Like supervised learning, contrastive learning beneﬁts
from deeper and wider networks.
We combine these ﬁndings to achieve a new state-of-the-art
in self-supervised and semi-supervised learning on Ima-
geNet ILSVRC-2012 (Russakovsky et al., 2015). Under the
linear evaluation protocol, SimCLR achieves 76.5% top-1
accuracy, which is a 7% relative improvement over previous
state-of-the-art (Hénaff et al., 2019). When ﬁne-tuned with
only 1% of the ImageNet labels, SimCLR achieves 85.8%
top-5 accuracy, a relative improvement of 10% (Hénaff et al.,
2019). When ﬁne-tuned on other natural image classiﬁca-
tion datasets, SimCLR performs on par with or better than
a strong supervised baseline (Kornblith et al., 2019) on 10
out of 12 datasets.

Discriminative approaches learn representations using objec-

trastive learning of visual representations, which we call
SimCLR . Not only does SimCLR outperform previous work

ized architectures (Bachman et al., 2019; Hénaff et al., 2019)
nor a memory bank (Wu et al., 2018; Tian et al., 2019; He
et al., 2019; Misra & van der Maaten, 2019).

A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
Ting Chen1Simon Kornblith1Mohammad Norouzi1Geoffrey Hinton1
Abstract
This paper presents SimCLR : a simple framework
for contrastive learning of visual representations.
We simplify recently proposed contrastive self-
supervised learning algorithms without requiring
specialized architectures or a memory bank. In
order to understand what enables the contrastive
prediction tasks to learn useful representations,
we systematically study the major components of
our framework. We show that (1) composition of
data augmentations plays a critical role in deﬁning
effective predictive tasks, (2) introducing a learn-
able nonlinear transformation between the repre-
sentation and the contrastive loss substantially im-
proves the quality of the learned representations,
and (3) contrastive learning beneﬁts from larger
batch sizes and more training steps compared to
supervised learning. By combining these ﬁndings,
we are able to considerably outperform previous
methods for self-supervised and semi-supervised
learning on ImageNet. A linear classiﬁer trained
on self-supervised representations learned by Sim-
CLR achieves 76.5% top-1 accuracy, which is a
7% relative improvement over previous state-of-
the-art, matching the performance of a supervised
ResNet-50. When ﬁne-tuned on only 1% of the
labels, we achieve 85.8% top-5 accuracy, outper-
forming AlexNet with 100 fewer labels.1
1. Introduction
Learning effective visual representations without human
supervision is a long-standing problem. Most mainstream
approaches fall into one of two classes: generative or dis-
criminative. Generative approaches learn to generate or
otherwise model pixels in the input space (Hinton et al.,
2006; Kingma & Welling, 2013; Goodfellow et al., 2014).

Statistical Signiﬁcance Testing We test for the signiﬁcance of differences between model with a permutation test. Given
predictions of two models, we generate 100,000 samples from the null distribution by randomly exchanging predictions
for each example and computing the difference in accuracy after performing this randomization. We then compute the
percentage of samples from the null distribution that are more extreme than the observed difference in predictions. For top-1
accuracy, this procedure yields the same result as the exact McNemar test. The assumption of exchangeability under the null
hypothesis is also valid for mean per-class accuracy, but not when computing average precision curves. Thus, we perform
signiﬁcance testing for a difference in accuracy on VOC 2007 rather than a difference in mAP. A caveat of this procedure is
that it does not consider run-to-run variability when training the models, only variability arising from using a ﬁnite sample
of images for evaluation.

of more domain-specific  information.6.2. Sensitivity  to frequency  mixing ratio 𝛽 in BFDA
The frequency  mixing ratio 𝛽 in BFDA is crucial for controlling  
the exchange  of low-frequency  components  between  domains,  thereby  
striking  a balance  between  structural  preservation  and style adaptation.  
To evaluate  its impact systematically,  we conducted  a sensitivity  analy-
sis on the MMWHS17  dataset,  varying  𝛽 from 0.05 to 1. As illustrated  in 
Fig.  9, adaptation  performance  demonstrates  a distinct  non-monotonic  
relationship  with 𝛽.

0.5 for the source domain  and 0.01 for the target domain,  while the 
enhancement  degree 𝑁 in spectral  regularization  was set to 30 for the 
source domain  and 10 for the target domain.
All models  were trained  using data derived  from the same pre-
processed  3D volumes.  We applied  an identical  pre-processing  pipeline  
(intensity  normalization  to [−1,1]) and the same set of data aug-

across all experiments.  For the 2D methods,  slices were consistently  
extracted  from these 3D volumes  following  the practice  established  
in DDSP (using coronal  slices for MMWHS17,  axial slices for BraTS21  
and PROMISE12).  Crucially,  to ensure all methods  were evaluated  on the same ultimate  task of 3D segmentation,  the predictions  from all

the training  setup, for the 2D methods,  we followed  the training

naturally  differ between  2D and 3D networks,  we reproduced  the 
baselines  in the same computing  environment  as proposed  in their 
original  work.
Evaluation  metrics:  To evaluate  segmentation  quality,  we employed  
two complementary  evaluation  criteria:  the Dice Similarity  Coefficient  
(DSC) and Average  Surface  Distance  (ASD). DSC quantifies  the spatial 
agreement  between  predicted  segmentations  and their corresponding  
ground  truth annotations,  with values spanning  from 0 (indicating  com-
plete mismatch)  to 1 (representing  perfect alignment).  ASD provides  a 
complementary  boundary-focused  perspective  by calculating  the mean

et al. (2025 ) recently  proposed  a domain  adaptive  detection  framework  
that integrates  feature and image alignment  with adversarial  learning  
to improve  the robustness  of multi-center  bone tumor detection  on 
radiographs.
2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.
2.4. Prior knowledge  constraint  methods
Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-
tropy over target data while incorporating  anatomical  priors via KL 
divergence.  This method  effectively  handles  scenarios  where source 
images are unavailable  due to privacy  constraints.  Diao et al. (2024 ) 
developed  TSANet,  a two-stage  pipeline  combining  Fourier-based  style 
transfer  with anatomical  entropy  minimization.  While improving  seg-
mentation  accuracy,  its adaptability  is limited  in domains  with sig-
nificant  structural  variations.  Gupta et al. (2022 ) incorporated  topo-
logical constraints  to enforce  geometric  relationships  between  organs,  
though  its reliance  on annotated  data to identify  and refine critical 
pixels restricts  its application  in fully unsupervised  settings.  Kervadec  et al. (2019 ) designed  a volume-based  regularization  term for weakly-
supervised  segmentation,  while Zhou et al. (2019 ) used statistical  label 
distributions  with KL divergence  guidance.  Zheng et al. (2024 ) pro-
posed DDSP, which builds upon feature disentanglement  with semantic  
consistency  and domain  perturbation  to improve  pseudo-label  quality.  
However,  these methods  generally  require  dataset-specific  pre-analysis  
or explicit  anatomical  constraints,  limiting  their flexibility  in handling  
dynamic  domain  shifts.
In contrast,  our FAUDA-Net  introduces  a frequency-aware  con-
trastive  alignment  mechanism  that captures  both structural  consistency  
and stylistic  variance  through  adaptive  frequency-domain  learning.  Un-
like methods  that depend  on pre-defined  spatial constraints  or dataset-
specific  statistical  priors, our approach  leverages  phase and amplitude  
representations  to achieve  non-rigid  and dynamic  feature alignment  
across domains.  By integrating  frequency-domain  cues with contrastive  
learning,  FAUDA-Net  aligns features  without  requiring  annotated  data 
in the target domain  or pre-computed  constraints,  enabling  robust

【来源：《1-s2.0-S0895611125001934-main.pdf》】
imal overhead  of 0.69G FLOPs (+1%), confirming  its lightweight  na-
ture as it operates  selectively  on phase components.  The complete  
FAUDA-Net  requires  65.54G  FLOPs and achieves  an inference  time of 
1.41 s. This indicates  a moderate  increase  compared  to DDSP (41.76G  
FLOPs, 0.90 s inference).  However,  we believe  this overhead  is jus-
tified for several reasons.  First, the inference  time of 1.41 s remains  
practical  for clinical  applications.  Second,  the additional  computation  
enables  substantial  performance  improvements  across all three chal-
lenging  datasets.  Third, the frequency-domain  operations  including  
frequency-aware  contrastive  learning  effectively  provide  more reliable  
cross-domain  alignment,  representing  a favorable  trade-off  for clinical  
deployment.
6.7. Limitation
Although  our method  has demonstrated  promising  results in various  
cross-domain  segmentation  tasks, several limitations  remain.  Firstly, 
the manual  setting of the range of 𝑁 in SR introduces  operational  
complexity.  The optimal  range for 𝑁 differs between  the source and 
target domains,  necessitating  iterative  search processes  to determine  
the optimal  settings.  This process  can consume  considerable  time and 
computational  resources,  particularly  when adapting  to new clinical  
domains  with distinct  imaging  characteristics.  Secondly,  we found that 
training  our model in a pre-training  manner  (i.e., training  on the source 
domain  data and fine-tuning  on the target domain  data) performs  very 
poorly.  This phenomenon  may stem from the inherent  limitations  of

per_question_results.question: CycleGAN 如何实现无配对图像到图像的翻译？
per_question_results.ground_truth: CycleGAN 通过循环一致性损失（cycle consistency loss）实现无配对图像翻译。它学习两个映射函数：G（从源域到目标域）和 F（从目标域到源域），并通过循环一致性损失确保 F(G(x)) 约等于 x，从而在无配对数据的情况下实现图像翻译。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问。关于CycleGAN如何实现无配对图像到图像的翻译，知识库中提供了明确的技术说明，我为您整理如下：

1. CycleGAN通过引入**对抗损失（adversarial loss）**和**循环一致性损失（cycle consistency loss）**来实现无配对数据下的图像翻译【来源：《CYCLEGAN.pdf》】。  
   - 对抗损失用于让生成器合成的图像在视觉上难以被判别器区分真假，从而逼真地模拟目标域风格；  
   - 循环一致性损失则强制要求：将源域图像x翻译为目标域图像y后，再将其翻译回源域，应尽可能还原为原始x（即G(F(y)) ≈ y 且 F(G(x)) ≈ x），以此保证内容一致性【来源：《Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf》】。

2. 具体架构包含两个生成器（G和F）和两个判别器（D_X和D_Y）：  
   - G将X域图像映射到Y域，F将Y域图像映射回X域；  
   - D_X判别真实X图像与F(Y)重建图像，D_Y判别真实Y图像与G(X)合成图像【来源：《CYCLEGAN.pdf》】。

The proposed framework consists of two main subnetworks:
(1) an image transformation subnetwork; (2) multi-teacher
knowledge distillation subnetwork. The first subnetwork is
used to transform the image from the source/target domain into
the target/source domain. The second subnetwork takes the
synthesized images as input to accomplish the segmentation
tasks. In the first subnetwork, MC-CCycleGAN is proposed
as the style transfer network, which introduces the contrastive
learning within the framework of CycleGAN. The contrastive
learning method is used to fully extract the structural features
of the input image in the generator’s encoder of MC-
CCycleGAN, while eliminate redundant style features. This
greatly improves MC-CCycleGAN’s ability to perform image
style transfer, reduces the style differences between different
domain images, and ensures the consistency of image content.

B. Contrastive Learning for Feature Alignment
CycleGAN has been able to generate fake images by
introducing adversarial learning at the image level. However,
when the domain shift is large, the encoder of the generator
in CycleGAN cannot fully extract the structural and style
features from the original image, which tends to result in the
inconsistency of the structure between the synthesized image
and the original image. To alleviate the problem, the encoder
of the generator is aimed to only extract the structural features
of the image while discard redundant style features, in order
to maintain consistency of the structure and content between
the synthesized image and the original image.

the synthesized image back to the original domain and the dierence between
this reconstructed image and the original image is added as a regularization term
during training.

Abstract — CT and MR are currently the most common
imaging techniques for pancreatic cancer diagnosis. Accu-
rate segmentation of the pancreas in CT and MR images
can provide significant help in the diagnosis and treatment
of pancreatic cancer. Traditional supervised segmentation
methods require a large number of labeled CT and MR train-
ing data, which is usually time-consuming and laborious.
Meanwhile, due to domain shift, traditional segmentation
networks are difficult to be deployed on different imag-
ing modality datasets. Cross-domain segmentation can
utilize labeled source domain data to assist unlabeled
target domains in solving the above problems. In this
paper, a cross-domain pancreas segmentation algorithm

Cycle Generative Adversarial Networks (MC-CCycleGAN).
MC-CCycleGAN is a style transfer network, in which the
encoder of its generator is used to extract features from real
images and style transfer images, constrain feature extrac-
tion through a contrastive loss, and fully extract structural
features of input images during style transfer while eliminate
redundant style features. The multi-order central moments
of the pancreas are proposed to describe its anatomy in
high dimensions and a contrastive loss is also proposed
to constrain the moment consistency, so as to maintain
consistency of the pancreatic structure and shape before

Due to its remarkable performance in reducing annotation

per_question_results.question: CaCo 方法如何利用类别对比进行无监督域适应？
per_question_results.ground_truth: CaCo（Category Contrast）将实例对比学习视为字典查找操作，构建了一个包含源域和目标域样本的语义感知字典，其中每个目标样本根据源样本的类别先验分配伪类别标签。通过类别对比学习（目标查询与类别级字典之间），实现类别判别性且域不变的特征表示。
per_question_results.source_doc: Category Contrast for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Visual Task.pdf
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问，很高兴为您解答关于CaCo方法的问题😊

CaCo（Category Contrast）方法通过引入**类别对比机制**来实现无监督域适应（UDA），其核心思想是：在不依赖目标域标签的前提下，利用源域的类别先验知识，构建一个**语义感知、跨域混合的类别字典**，并在此基础上进行类别级的对比学习。具体来说，它通过以下方式实现：

1. **构建类别感知且跨域混合的字典**：CaCo从源域和目标域中共同采样样本，为每个目标样本分配基于源域类别先验的（伪）类别标签，并据此构建一个“类别-aware且domain-mixed”的字典K = {k₁, k₂, ..., k_C}，其中每个k_c代表第c类的键（key）集合【来源：《Category Contrast for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Visual Task.pdf》】。

2. **执行类别对比损失（CatNCE）**：对未标注的目标查询样本x_q，CaCo计算其特征q = f_q(x_q)与字典中同类别键（正样本）的相似度，并拉近；同时推远与不同类别键（负样本）的距离。该损失函数确保：**同类样本（无论来自源域或目标域）在特征空间中被拉近，异类样本被推远**，从而学习到类别判别性强且域不变的特征表示【来源：《Category Contrast for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Visual Task.pdf》】。

3. **实现三重优势**：
   - 同时最小化类内差异、最大化类间距离（得益于类别感知字典）；
   - 实现域内与跨域对齐（得益于源域+目标域混合字典）；
   - 缓解数据不平衡问题（因字典按类别均衡构建，各类别键数量一致）【来源：《Category Contrast for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Visual Task.pdf》】。

此外，实验验证表明，CaCo不仅在分割、检测、分类等多类视觉UDA任务上均取得优于现有方法的性能，还能作为即插即用模块显著提升其他UDA方法（如CRST、CBST、FDA等）的效果，体现其强互补性与泛化性【来源：《Category Contrast for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Visual Task.pdf》】。

如您想了解CaCo在某类具体任务（如Cityscapes分割）中的性能细节，或希望获取公式/图示说明，欢迎随时告诉我，我可以为您进一步梳理～

Abstract
Instance contrast for unsupervised representation learn-
ing has achieved great success in recent years. In this
work, we explore the idea of instance contrastive learn-
ing in unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) and pro-
pose a novel Category Contrast technique (CaCo) that in-
troduces semantic priors on top of instance discrimination
for visual UDA tasks. By considering instance contrastive
learning as a dictionary look-up operation, we construct a
semantics-aware dictionary with samples from both source
and target domains where each target sample is assigned
a (pseudo) category label based on the category priors of
source samples. This allows category contrastive learn-
ing (between target queries and the category-level dictio-
nary) for category-discriminative yet domain-invariant fea-
ture representations: samples of the same category (from ei-
ther source or target domain) are pulled closer while those
of different categories are pushed apart simultaneously. Ex-
tensive UDA experiments in multiple visual tasks ( e:g:, seg-
mentation, classiﬁcation and detection) show that CaCo
achieves superior performance as compared with state-of-
the-art methods. The experiments also demonstrate that
CaCo is complementary to existing UDA methods and gen-
eralizable to other learning setups such as unsupervised
model adaptation, open-/partial-set adaptation etc.
1. Introduction
Though deep neural networks (DNNs) [20,56] have rev-
olutionized various computer vision tasks [4, 20, 46, 56],
they often generalize poorly to new domains due to do-
main gaps . Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims
to mitigate the domain gaps by exploiting unlabelled target-
domain data. To this end, researchers have designed differ-

【来源：《Category Contrast for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Visual Task.pdf》】
gory contrastive loss LCatNCE between target queries and
dictionary keys: samples of the same category are pulled
close while those of different categories are pushed away.
This naturally leads to category-discriminative yet domain-
invariant representations, which is perfectly aligned with
the objective of UDA.
With the category-aware and domain-mixed dictionary
together with the category contrastive loss, the proposed
Category Contrast tackles the UDA challenges with three
desirable features: 1) It concurrently minimizes the intra-
category variation and maximizes the inter-category dis-
tance with the category-aware dictionary design; 2) It
achieves inter-domain and intra-domain alignment simul-
taneously thanks to the domain-mixed dictionary design by
including both source and target samples; 3) It greatly mit-
igates the data balance issue due to the category-balanced
dictionary design which allows to compute contrast losses
evenly across all categories during learning.
The contributions of this work can be summarized
in three aspects. First , we investigate instance con-
trast for unsupervised domain adaptation, aiming to learn
discriminative representation for unlabelled target-domain
data. Second , we propose Category Contrast that builds a
category-aware and domain-mixed dictionary with a cat-
egory contrastive loss. It encourages to learn category-
discriminative yet domain-invariant representation which is
naturally aligned with the objective of UDA. Third , exten-
sive experiments show that the proposed CaCo achieves
superior UDA performance consistently as compared with
state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, CaCo is comple-
mentary with existing UDA methods and generalizable to
other learning setups that involves unlabeled data.2. Related Works
Our work is closely related to two main branches of re-
search, namely, unsupervised learning in unsupervised do-
main adaptation and instance contrast in unsupervised rep-
resentation learning.

On the other hand, existing instance contrastive learn-

UDA: 1). With little category priors, existing instance con-

level discrimination including various visual UDA tasks.
The proposed CaCo introduces a categorical domain-mixed
dictionary which introduces category priors and addresses
the two problems effectively.

Unsupervised domain adaptation aims to leverage un-
labelled target data to improve network performance in tar-
get domain. To learn from unlabelled target data, most ex-
isting works propose different unsupervised losses which
can be broadly classiﬁed into three categories. The ﬁrst
category is adversarial loss that enforces source-like tar-
get representation in the feature [7, 16, 37, 51, 61, 75], out-
put [28,39,50,52,58] or latent space [29,59,62]. The second
category is image translation loss that generates source data
with target-like styles and appearance via GANs [8, 10, 35]
and spectrum matching [25, 71]. The third category is
self-training loss that re-trains the network iteratively with
pseudo-labelled target samples [14,24,26,35,63,71,80,81].
We tackle UDA from a new perspective of instance con-
trastive learning, and propose a novel Category Contrast
(CaCo) that introduces a generic category contrastive loss
that can work for various UDA tasks. To the best of our
knowledge, this is the ﬁrst work that explores instance con-
trastive learning for UDA.
Instance Contrastive Learning [5, 19, 41, 57, 67, 72]
aims to learn an embedding space where positive sam-
ples are pulled close to an anchor and negative samples
are pushed away. Despite different motivations, instance
contrastive learning can be viewed as a dictionary look-up
task [19] that trains a visual encoder by matching an en-
coded query qwith a dictionary of encoded keys k:qshould
be similar to positive kand dissimilar to negative k. Three
typical dictionary creation strategies have been proposed.
The ﬁrst builds a memory bank [67] that stores the keys of
all samples in the previous epoch. The second creates an
end-to-end dictionary [5, 57, 72] that generates keys from
samples of the current mini-batch. The third employs a mo-
mentum encoder [19] that encodes samples on-the-ﬂy by a
momentum-updated encoder. Instance contrastive learning
with various dictionaries helps to learn better unsupervised
representations clearly.

that integrates  feature and image alignment  with adversarial  learning

2.3. Disentangled  representation  learning  methods
Disentangled  representation  learning  achieves  domain  adaptation  
by embedding  images into separate  domain-invariant  content  and 
domain-specific  style spaces. For instance,  Pei et al. (2021 ) proposed  
a UDA framework  that decomposes  domains  into invariant  and specific  
features,  using iterative  decoding  and encoding  to maintain  anatomical  
consistency  alongside  adversarial  discriminators.  Xie et al. (2022 ) 
integrated  self-supervised  learning  with disentangled  representations  
to further improve  segmentation  through  pseudo-labeling.  However,  
its limited  capacity  for modeling  feature diversity  can lead to over-
concentrated  representations.  Özbey et al. (2023 ) developed  UNIT-
DDPM,  integrating  diffusion  models  with adversarial  learning  to lever-
age reverse  diffusion  dynamics  for cross-domain  feature projection.  
This approach  captures  complex  domain  characteristics  and enhances  
alignment  stability  while mitigating  mode collapse.  Stan and Ros-
tami (2024 ) proposed  SFS, which combines  optimal  transport  with 
adversarial  strategies  to align features  in a shared space, improving  
performance  on unseen target distributions.  Despite  these advances,  
most disentangled  methods  rely on adversarial  mechanisms  and remain 
susceptible  to GAN-related  instability  and training  challenges.
2.4. Prior knowledge  constraint  methods
Medical  images contain  strong anatomical  priors such as organ 
shapes,  sizes, and spatial relationships,  which provide  valuable  con-
straints  for domain  adaptation.  Bateson  et al. (2022 ) introduced  a 
source-free  domain  adaptation  (SFDA)  approach  that minimizes  en-

divergence.  This method  effectively  handles  scenarios  where source 
images are unavailable  due to privacy  constraints.  Diao et al. (2024 ) 
developed  TSANet,  a two-stage  pipeline  combining  Fourier-based  style 
transfer  with anatomical  entropy  minimization.  While improving  seg-
mentation  accuracy,  its adaptability  is limited  in domains  with sig-
nificant  structural  variations.  Gupta et al. (2022 ) incorporated  topo-
logical constraints  to enforce  geometric  relationships  between  organs,  
though  its reliance  on annotated  data to identify  and refine critical 
pixels restricts  its application  in fully unsupervised  settings.  Kervadec  et al. (2019 ) designed  a volume-based  regularization  term for weakly-
supervised  segmentation,  while Zhou et al. (2019 ) used statistical  label 
distributions  with KL divergence  guidance.  Zheng et al. (2024 ) pro-
posed DDSP, which builds upon feature disentanglement  with semantic  
consistency  and domain  perturbation  to improve  pseudo-label  quality.  
However,  these methods  generally  require  dataset-specific  pre-analysis  
or explicit  anatomical  constraints,  limiting  their flexibility  in handling  
dynamic  domain  shifts.
In contrast,  our FAUDA-Net  introduces  a frequency-aware  con-
trastive  alignment  mechanism  that captures  both structural  consistency  
and stylistic  variance  through  adaptive  frequency-domain  learning.  Un-
like methods  that depend  on pre-defined  spatial constraints  or dataset-
specific  statistical  priors, our approach  leverages  phase and amplitude  
representations  to achieve  non-rigid  and dynamic  feature alignment  
across domains.  By integrating  frequency-domain  cues with contrastive  
learning,  FAUDA-Net  aligns features  without  requiring  annotated  data 
in the target domain  or pre-computed  constraints,  enabling  robust

per_question_results.question: 为什么 Deep MR to CT Synthesis 方法使用无配对数据训练？
per_question_results.ground_truth: 因为配对的 MR 和 CT 图像可能存在不对齐问题，这会导致合成 CT 图像时出现错误。使用无配对数据和循环一致性损失训练的 GAN 可以避免这个问题，生成更准确的合成 CT 图像。
per_question_results.source_doc: Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问。关于“Deep MR to CT Synthesis 方法为何使用无配对数据训练”，知识库中给出了明确的科学依据，我为您简要说明如下：

1. **避免图像配准误差带来的合成偏差**：传统方法依赖成对（paired）且空间对齐的MR和CT图像进行训练，但即使经过刚性配准，局部区域（如喉部、口腔、椎骨、鼻腔等）仍存在明显错位，这种错位会导致合成CT图像出现模糊或伪影【来源：《Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf》】。

2. **提升模型鲁棒性与泛化能力**：使用无配对（unpaired）数据训练可使模型不依赖于精确的空间对应关系，从而绕过配准失败的风险；研究显示，该方法在定量评估中MAE为73.7±2.3 HU，PSNR为32.3±0.7，显著优于使用配对数据训练的模型（p<0.05）【来源：《Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf》】。

3. **解决临床数据获取难题**：现实中，同一患者同时拥有高质量、严格对齐的MR和CT扫描的情况有限；而单模态扫描（如仅做MR或仅做CT）的数据更丰富。使用无配对数据可充分利用这些分散采集的影像资源，缓解训练数据稀缺问题【来源：《Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf》】。

4. **技术实现基础可靠**：该方法基于CycleGAN框架，通过对抗损失（adversarial loss）和循环一致性损失（cycle consistency loss）联合约束，确保MR→CT→MR的双向转换保持结构一致性，无需像素级标签监督【来源：《Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf》】。

如您想进一步了解模型架构细节、评估指标含义，或该方法在其他解剖部位（如胰腺、心脏）的应用情况，也欢迎随时告诉我，我可以为您补充说明。需要人工客服协助时，我也很乐意为您转接 😊

Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data
Jelmer M. Wolterink1�, Anna M. Dinkla2, Mark H.F. Savenije2,
Peter R. Seevinck1, Cornelis A.T. van den Berg2, Ivana I sgum1
1Image Sciences Institute, University Medical Center Utrecht, The Netherlands
j.m.wolterink@umcutrecht.nl
2Department of Radiotherapy, University Medical Center Utrecht, The Netherlands
Abstract. MR-only radiotherapy treatment planning requires accurate
MR-to-CT synthesis. Current deep learning methods for MR-to-CT syn-
thesis depend on pairwise aligned MR and CT training images of the
same patient. However, misalignment between paired images could lead
to errors in synthesized CT images. To overcome this, we propose to train
a generative adversarial network (GAN) with unpaired MR and CT im-
ages. A GAN consisting of two synthesis convolutional neural networks
(CNNs) and two discriminator CNNs was trained with cycle consistency
to transform 2D brain MR image slices into 2D brain CT image slices
and vice versa. Brain MR and CT images of 24 patients were analyzed.
A quantitative evaluation showed that the model was able to synthesize
CT images that closely approximate reference CT images, and was able
to outperform a GAN model trained with paired MR and CT images.
Keywords: Deep learning, radiotherapy, treatment planning, CT syn-
thesis, Generative Adversarial Networks
1 Introduction
Radiotherapy treatment planning requires a magnetic resonance (MR) volume
for segmentation of tumor volume and organs at risk, as well as a spatially
corresponding computed tomography (CT) volume for dose planning. Separate
acquisition of these volumes is time-consuming, costly and a burden to the pa-
tient. Furthermore, voxel-wise spatial alignment between MR and CT images
may be compromised, requiring accurate registration of MR and CT volumes.
Hence, to circumvent separate CT acquisition, a range of methods have been
proposed for MR-only radiotherapy treatment planning in which a substitute or
synthetic CT image is derived from the available MR image [2].

【来源：《Deep MR to CT Synthesis using Unpaired Data.pdf》】
learning-based CT synthesis systems (Fig. 1).
Recently, methods have been proposed to train image-to-image translation
CNNs with unpaired natural images, namely DualGAN [11] and CycleGAN [12].
Like the methods proposed in [4,8,9], these CNNs translate an image from one
domain to another domain. Unlike these methods, the loss function during train-
ing depends solely on the overall quality of the synthesized image as determined
by an adversarial discriminator network. To prevent the synthesis CNN from
generating images that look real but bear little similarity to the input image,
cycle consistency is enforced. That is, an additional CNN is trained to translate
the synthesized image back to the original domain and the dierence between
this reconstructed image and the original image is added as a regularization term
during training.
Here, we use a CycleGAN model to synthesize brain CT images from brain
MR images. We show that training with pairs of spatially aligned MR and CT
images of the same patients is not necessary for deep learning-based CT synthe-
sis.

for radiotherapy treatment planning of brain tumors. MR and CT images were

5 Discussion and Conclusion
We have shown that a CNN can be trained to synthesize a CT image from
an MR image using unpaired and unaligned MR and CT training images. In
contrast to previous work, the model learns to synthesize realistically-looking
images guided only by the performance of an adversarial discriminator network
and the similarity of back-transformed output images to the original input image.

3 Methods
The CycleGAN model proposed by Zhu et al. and used in this work contains a
forward and a backward cycle (Fig. 3) [12].
The forward cycle consists of three separate CNNs. First, network SynCTis
trained to translate an input MR image IMRinto a CT image. Second, network
SynMRis trained to translate a synthesized CT image SynCT(IMR) back into an
4 J.M. Wolterink et al.
MR image. Third, network DisCTis trained to discriminate between synthesized
SynCT(IMR) and real CT images ICT. Each of these three neural networks has
a dierent goal. While DisCTaims to distinguish synthesized CT images from
real CT images, network SynCTtries to prevent this by synthesizing images
that cannot be distinguished from real CT images. These images should be
translated back to the MR domain by network SynMRso that the original
image is reconstructed from SynCT(IMR) as accurately as possible.
To improve training stability, the backward cycle is also trained, translating
CT images into MR images and back into CT images. For synthesis, this model
uses the same CNNs SynCTandSynMR. In addition, it contains a discriminator
networkDisMRthat aims to distinguish synthesized MR images from real MR
images.

I. INTRODUCTION
PANCREATIC cancer has strong concealment, rapid onset,
and high malignancy. Its five-year survival rate is only
5%-10%, and hence it is called the “king of cancers”. Accord-
ing to the American Cancer Annual Report [1]in 2020, a total
of 57,600 people were diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, and
47,050 people died of pancreatic cancer. Pancreatic cancer has
become one of worldwide cancers, and early detection plays
a crucial role in its treatment.
Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance
(MR) are two common imaging techniques for pancreatic
cancer [2]. The imaging principles of CT and MR result in
large modality differences. CT images typically show uniform
intensity distribution and strong contrast, with clear tissue
boundaries and contours. In contrast, MR images usually have
uneven intensity distribution and relatively indistinct tissue
boundaries and contours. CT and MR have different imaging
expressions for the pancreas, providing doctors with reliable
data support for making accurate diagnosis from different
modalities.
Deep neural networks have achieved great success in pan-
creas segmentation [3],[4], when the training and testing data
are drawn from the same distribution. These works require a
large amount of annotated data. However, acquiring such a
large amount of data is time-consuming and labor-intensive,
especially for medical images that require diagnostic expertise
[5]. It has been pointed out that well-trained models often
fail when tested on data from different modalities, as medical
images acquired from different modalities have very different
characteristics [6],[7],[8],[9]. Severe domain shift between
modalities usually reduces the performance of well-trained
deep neural networks. Although it is easy for human to

V. D ISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION
In this paper, MC-CCycleGAN is proposed for cross-
domain pancreas segmentation. The structure and shape of
the pancreas are well preserved through our method, which
significantly improves the segmentation performance. The
results presented in the previous sections have demonstrated
the effectiveness and superiority of our method.
Kindly note that the proposed framework for cross-domain
pancreas segmentation is a kind of unsupervised domain
adaptation, in which the source domain images are provided
with segmentation labels but the target domain images are
not provided with segmentation labels in the training stage.
Although the scenario is called unsupervised domain adapta-
tion, it is indeed a kind of semi-supervised learning, which
needs the labels of source domain images for cross-domain
adaptation.
Unsupervised domain adaptation aims to utilize labeled
source domain images to adapt to the target domain without
using additional annotations from the target domain. Cycle-
GAN is often employed for unsupervised domain adaptation

【来源：《Moment-Consistent_Contrastive_CycleGAN_for_Cross-Domain_Pancreatic_Image_Segmentation.pdf》】
domain images, and ensures the consistency of image content.
In order to maintain the consistency of the structure and shape
of the pancreas in both the original and synthesized images,
the multi-order central moments of the pancreas are computed
to provide a high-dimensional description of its anatomy,
and perform contrastive learning on the consistent moments.
In the second subnetwork, a multi-teacher knowledge dis-
tillation framework is proposed for target domain pancreas
segmentation. Multi-teacher models are pre-trained using syn-
thesized images generated by MC-CCycleGAN from different
training epochs. With this framework, the model is compressed
by transferring the knowledge from multiple teachers to a
single student model. Comprehensive experiments have been
performed with one in-house dataset: Multi-Modality Pancreas
Segmentation (MMPS) dataset, and two publicly available
datasets: Abdominal Multi-Organ Benchmark for Versatile
Medical Image Segmentation(AMOS) and Multi-Modality
Whole Heart Segmentation (MMWHS) Challenge 2017. The
experimental results have demonstrated the superiority of our
framework over state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods.
Our main contributions are summarized as,
1. CCycleGAN is proposed to preserve the structural fea-
tures of images and remove excessive style features during
image style transfer.
2. Multi-order central moments are integrated into CCy-
cleGAN to describe its anatomy in high dimension and a
contrastive loss is proposed to ensure the consistency of the
multi-order central moments, so as to maintain consistency of
the structure and shape before and after style transfer.
3. A multi-teacher knowledge distillation framework is
proposed to transfer the knowledge from multiple teachers to
a single student model.
II. R ELATED WORK
Many pancreas segmentation methods [3], [4], [15], [16]
have been proposed for CT and MR images. However, due
to the huge difference between CT and MR images, these
methods often failed in cross-domain (CT to MR or MR

per_question_results.question: Distill-SODA 如何应对计算病理学中的开放集域适应问题？
per_question_results.ground_truth: Distill-SODA 通过从自监督 Vision Transformer 中提取知识，引入基于风格的对抗数据增强作为硬正例，对 ViT 进行自训练。然后将语义相似的目标图像聚类，利用源模型提供弱监督，从而同时处理未知类别的语义偏移和协变量偏移（颜色外观变化）。
per_question_results.answer:
您好！感谢您的提问。作为专业客服，我很乐意为您介绍Distill-SODA如何应对计算病理学中的开放集域适应（SF-OSDA）问题。以下回答严格依据知识库内容：

1. Distill-SODA 是一种专为**源端无数据、开放集场景**设计的域适应方法，旨在同时应对两类关键挑战：  
   - **语义偏移**（即目标域中存在源域未见过的新组织类别，如c-STR、DEB、ADI等）【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】；  
   - **协变量偏移**（即相同组织类型在不同染色/扫描设备下呈现的颜色/外观差异）【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】。

2. 其核心技术路径分为三步：  
   - **知识蒸馏**：利用自监督视觉Transformer（ViT）——如DINO、CTransPath或经风格对抗增强（AdvStyle）自训练的ViT——为无标签目标域图像生成高质量、上下文化强的特征嵌入，从而弥补源模型在分布偏移下的表征退化【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】；  
   - **伪标签优化**：提出“闭集亲和度分数”（CSAS），在ViT嵌入空间中对源模型产生的弱伪标签进行置信度校准，并据此计算加权类原型，显著提升伪标签可靠性【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】；  
   - **模型适配**：使用l₂损失函数对源模型进行轻量级自蒸馏式微调，该损失能更好保留最大logit分数（MLS）的置信度排序能力，从而同步提升闭集准确率（ACC）与开放集检测能力（AUC）【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】。

3. 实验验证表明：  
   - Distill-SODA（CE+）在三个结直肠癌组织数据集（Kather-16/Kather-19/CRCTP）上全面超越SOTA方法，平均ACC提升+14.2%，AUC提升+18.3%【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】；  
   - 仅需3.5k（5%）目标域图像即可超越其他方法使用全部70k图像的性能，具备临床落地所需的低数据依赖性与高效性【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】；  
   - 方法对源模型架构（MobileNet-V2、ResNet18、ViT等）不敏感，且可无缝集成CE+、MC-Dropout、T3PO等多种开放集检测策略，增强其泛化鲁棒性【来源：《Distill-SODA.pdf》】。

如您想了解具体技术实现细节（如AdvStyle增强策略、CSAS公式推导）或某组实验结果的解读，欢迎随时告诉我，我将为您进一步说明。若涉及模型部署、参数调优等实操问题，建议转接我们的技术工程师为您提供一对一支持。😊

VI. C ONCLUSION
We introduced Distill-SODA , a novel approach in source-free
open-set domain adaptation designed to boost model resilience
against both semantic and covariate shifts for histopathological
image analysis. The core innovation lies in the knowledge
transfer from a self-supervised vision transformer to the source
model, specifically tailored to adapt when faced with open-set
scenarios in the target domain. We have demonstrated that
Distill-SODA is not only compatible with existing pre-trained
vision transformers but also excels when employed with public
histopathology or specific target datasets. Additionally, we
propose a novel style-based adversarial augmentation strategy
11
that further refines the self-training of vision transformers
directly on the target dataset.
Our approach has consistently outperformed multiple state-
of-the-art baselines, especially in the context of three colorectal

II. R ELATED WORK
A. Open-Set Detection
In an open-set setting, a trained model must be able to
discriminate known (closed-set) from unknown categories
(open-set) that have not yet been encountered. There are a
few subcategories of open-set recognition approaches. The first
is model activation rectification strategies [20], [21], where
open-set examples can be detected using a rectification scheme
for the activation patterns of the model related to closed-set
examples. Other approaches utilize GANs to generate images
resembling open-set samples [22] or train GAN-discriminator
to distinguish closed from open-set samples [23]. Seminal work
[9] demonstrates that robust classifiers with high closed-set
accuracy also serve as better open-set detectors. The authors
establish Maximum Logit Score (MLS) as a baseline open-
set scoring metric for distinguishing known from unknown
classes. Motivated by this, our method uses un-normalized
logits for model adaptation and open-set recognition instead
of the softmax output probabilities.
Other methods, such as Monte Carlo Dropout or Multi-head
CNN-based models [24], [25], measure uncertainty during
inference to recognize open-set images with high uncertainty.

namely a source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) setting, where

Several SFDA methods [4], [5] have been proposed en route

Nonetheless, for every new dataset, these methods necessitate
